items.title: Improve Codex's Long-Term Project Maintenance: Edit in Place and Proactive Cleanup

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: model-behavior
labels.description: Issues related to behaviors exhibited by the model

items.body:
I've noticed a significant difference between Claude Code and OpenAI Codex when working on long-running research projects, particularly neuroimaging and scientific computing workflows.

Claude Code tends to modify existing scripts and files directly rather than creating new directories or files for each iteration. When certain files or folders are explicitly identified as unnecessary, it also removes them, helping keep the project organized.

In contrast, Codex frequently generates new directories and file versions, even when the task is simply to revise an existing analysis. After repeated iterations, this results in a proliferation of redundant scripts, outdated results, and unnecessary folders.

This is particularly problematic in neuroimaging research, where analyses often require extensive revisions and generate large intermediate datasets.

Suggested improvements:

Default to modifying existing scripts and files rather than creating new versions.

Reuse the existing project structure whenever possible.

Proactively identify obsolete files, redundant outputs, and unnecessary directories.

Remove explicitly discarded files when authorized, while protecting raw data and validated research outputs.

Treat project organization and cleanliness as part of successful task completion.

The key principle: Codex should maintain and improve an existing project, not continuously expand its file structure with every iteration.

This would substantially improve Codex's usability for long-term scientific research and other complex coding projects.

items.title: [Windows desktop] Responses HTTP fallback remains latched across turns after WebSocket/server errors (Codex and Work)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

items.body:
## Problem

The Windows desktop-bundled native client can remain on HTTP for all later turns after a transient WebSocket failure or a generic server error. A healthy WebSocket endpoint is not retried in the existing chat; a fresh ephemeral chat in the same process uses it successfully.

This is a deterministic client-state reproduction, separate from the upstream cause of any real network or inference error. It reproduces with both `Codex Desktop` and `codex_work_desktop` originators.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Home build 26300, x64.
- Desktop product 26.1007.21434, build 13901, production channel; Windows package 26.1007.2314.0.
- Bundled `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2`.
- Configured desktop updater reports `up_to_date`.
- Python 3.11 and aiohttp 3.13.3 for the mock.

## Reproduction

The script below uses a localhost-only mock, an explicit dummy API key, command-line-only provider settings, and ephemeral chats. It does not require OpenAI inference or research history. It creates no saved provider or persistent mock chats.

1. Chat A opens WebSockets. The mock either closes them or returns a generic `500 server_error`.
2. Codex exhausts the test retry budget and falls back to HTTP SSE, which completes successfully.
3. The mock makes WebSockets healthy.
4. A new turn in chat A still uses HTTP, with **zero WebSocket requests**.
5. A fresh chat B in the same process uses WebSockets, with **zero HTTP requests**.

Observed counters (WebSocket counts include warmup):

| Stage | WebSocket requests | HTTP requests |
|---|---:|---:|
| Chat A, initial failure/fallback | 3 | 1 |
| Chat A, next turn after recovery | 0 | 1 |
| Fresh chat B control | 2 | 0 |

Commands:

```text
python repro_transport_fallback.py --client codex --failure disconnect
python repro_transport_fallback.py --client work --failure disconnect
python repro_transport_fallback.py --client codex --failure server-error --assert-recovery
python repro_transport_fallback.py --client work --failure server-error --assert-recovery
```

`--assert-recovery` fails on the installed client with `RECOVERY_REGRESSION: the existing thread remained on HTTP after WebSockets recovered`.

Disabling `unbounded_connection_retries` did not change the behavior. An explicit `503 server_is_overloaded` was a useful counterexample: it produced `serverOverloaded` without fallback. Generic server errors and explicitly classified overload must therefore be distinguished.

## Source correlation and requested change

The current upstream source explicitly makes the fallback session-scoped:

- [ModelClient fallback state and documentation](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a07c8ebd57feedc4cf5dfe854c8e9101de54186b/codex-rs/core/src/client.rs#L256)
- [force_http_fallback sets disable_websockets](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a07c8ebd57feedc4cf5dfe854c8e9101de54186b/codex-rs/core/src/client.rs#L714)
- [Retry-budget exhaustion switches transport](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a07c8ebd57feedc4cf5dfe854c8e9101de54186b/codex-rs/core/src/responses_retry.rs#L120)

Please consider bounded re-probing on a later turn or after a cooldown, and avoiding transport downgrade when the failure only establishes a model-server error. Recovery should preserve context and existing work without requiring manual compaction or archive/restore.

Related reports: #45971 and #53127. This adds a minimal, deterministic, credential-free reproduction of the fallback lifetime; it does not establish that every symptom in those reports has the same upstream cause.

<details>
<summary>repro_transport_fallback.py</summary>

```python
"""Exercise the installed Codex transport against a local, credential-free mock."""
import asyncio
import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import tomllib

from aiohttp import web


def response_events(text, number):
    response_id = f"resp_local_{number}"
    item = {"id": f"msg_local_{number}", "type": "message", "role": "assistant",
            "status": "completed", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": text, "annotations": []}]}
    return [
        {"type": "response.created", "response": {"id": response_id, "status": "in_progress"}},
        {"type": "response.output_item.added", "output_index": 0, "item": {**item, "content": []}},
        {"type": "response.output_text.delta", "item_id": item["id"], "output_index": 0,
         "content_index": 0, "delta": text},
        {"type": "response.output_item.done", "output_index": 0, "item": item},
        {"type": "response.completed", "response": {"id": response_id, "status": "completed",
         "output": [item], "usage": {"input_tokens": 1, "output_tokens": 1, "total_tokens": 2,
         "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}}}},
    ]


async def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--client", choices=("codex", "work"), default="codex")
    parser.add_argument("--failure", choices=("disconnect", "overload", "server-error"), default="disconnect")
    parser.add_argument("--bounded-connection-retries", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--assert-recovery", action="store_true",
                        help="Fail if a later healthy turn remains on HTTP; use to validate a client fix.")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    executable = shutil.which("codex.exe")
    if not executable:
        raise SystemExit("codex.exe is not on PATH")
    config_path = Path.home() / ".codex" / "config.toml"
    config = tomllib.loads(config_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    state = {"healthy": False, "ws_requests": 0, "http_requests": 0}

    async def endpoint(request):
        # Explicit dummy provider credentials prevent using the signed-in account.
        if request.headers.get("Authorization") != "Bearer local-diagnostic-only":
            raise web.HTTPForbidden(text="Expected diagnostic-only credentials")
        if request.headers.get("Upgrade", "").lower() == "websocket":
            socket = web.WebSocketResponse()
            await socket.prepare(request)
            async for message in socket:
                if message.type != web.WSMsgType.TEXT:
                    continue
                state["ws_requests"] += 1
                if not state["healthy"]:
                    if args.failure in ("overload", "server-error"):
                        overloaded = args.failure == "overload"
                        await socket.send_json({"type": "error", "status": 503 if overloaded else 500, "error": {
                            "type": "service_unavailable_error" if overloaded else "server_error",
                            "code": "server_is_overloaded" if overloaded else "server_error",
                            "message": "We are currently experiencing high demand, which may cause temporary errors."}})
                        continue
                    await socket.close()
                    break
                for event in response_events("WEBSOCKET_OK", state["ws_requests"]):
                    await socket.send_json(event)
            return socket
        if request.method == "POST":
            await request.read()
            state["http_requests"] += 1
            body = "".join("data: " + json.dumps(e) + "\n\n"
                           for e in response_events("HTTP_FALLBACK", state["http_requests"]))
            return web.Response(text=body, content_type="text/event-stream")
        raise web.HTTPNotFound()

    app = web.Application(client_max_size=20 * 1024 * 1024)
    app.router.add_route("*", "/v1/responses", endpoint)
    runner = web.AppRunner(app, access_log=None)
    await runner.setup()
    site = web.TCPSite(runner, "127.0.0.1", 0)
    await site.start()
    port = site._server.sockets[0].getsockname()[1]
    command = [executable, "app-server", "--stdio"]
    for feature in ("plugins", "apps", "hooks", "multi_agent", "multi_agent_v2", "shell_tool"):
        command += ["--disable", feature]
    if args.bounded_connection_retries:
        command += ["--disable", "unbounded_connection_retries"]
    overrides = {
        "model_provider": "local-transport-test",
        "model_providers.local-transport-test.name": "Local transport test",
        "model_providers.local-transport-test.base_url": f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/v1",
        "model_providers.local-transport-test.env_key": "CODEX_DIAGNOSTIC_DUMMY_KEY",
        "model_providers.local-transport-test.supports_websockets": True,
        "model_providers.local-transport-test.stream_max_retries": 1,
        "model_providers.local-transport-test.request_max_retries": 0,
        "model_providers.local-transport-test.stream_idle_timeout_ms": 10000,
        "analytics.enabled": False,
        "notify": [],
    }
    overrides.update({f"mcp_servers.{name}.enabled": False for name in config.get("mcp_servers", {})})
    for key, value in overrides.items():
        command += ["-c", key + "=" + json.dumps(value)]
    environment = os.environ.copy()
    environment["CODEX_DIAGNOSTIC_DUMMY_KEY"] = "local-diagnostic-only"
    environment["CODEX_INTERNAL_ORIGINATOR_OVERRIDE"] = "codex_work_desktop" if args.client == "work" else "Codex Desktop"
    environment["RUST_LOG"] = "warn,codex_api::endpoint::responses_websocket=info,codex_core::client=trace"
    process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(*command, stdin=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
        stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, env=environment,
        creationflags=0x08000000, limit=4 * 1024 * 1024)
    stderr_task = asyncio.create_task(process.stderr.read())
    inbox = asyncio.Queue()
    notifications = []

    async def read_messages():
        async for line in process.stdout:
            message = json.loads(line)
            if "id" in message and "method" not in message:
                await inbox.put(message)
            elif message.get("method") == "turn/completed":
                await inbox.put(message)
            else:
                notifications.append(message.get("method"))

    reader = asyncio.create_task(read_messages())

    async def send(method, params, request_id=None):
        message = {"method": method, "params": params}
        if request_id is not None:
            message["id"] = request_id
        process.stdin.write((json.dumps(message) + "\n").encode())
        await process.stdin.drain()
        if request_id is None:
            return None
        while True:
            result = await asyncio.wait_for(inbox.get(), 25)
            if result.get("id") == request_id:
                if "error" in result:
                    raise RuntimeError(json.dumps(result["error"]))
                return result["result"]

    async def start_thread(number):
        result = await send("thread/start", {"model": "gpt-6-astra", "ephemeral": True,
            "approvalPolicy": "never", "sandbox": "read-only",
            "baseInstructions": "This is a local transport protocol test."}, number)
        return result["thread"]["id"]

    async def turn(thread_id, number):
        before = dict(state)
        result = await send("turn/start", {"threadId": thread_id,
            "input": [{"type": "text", "text": "Return a diagnostic marker."}]}, number)
        turn_id = result["turn"]["id"]
        while True:
            message = await asyncio.wait_for(inbox.get(), 25)
            if message.get("method") == "turn/completed" and message["params"]["turn"]["id"] == turn_id:
                status = message["params"]["turn"]["status"]
                return {"status": status, "ws_requests": state["ws_requests"] - before["ws_requests"],
                        "http_requests": state["http_requests"] - before["http_requests"],
                        "error": message["params"]["turn"].get("error")}

    try:
        await send("initialize", {"clientInfo": {"name": "local_transport_diagnostic", "version": "1.0"},
                                  "capabilities": {"experimentalApi": True}}, 1)
        await send("initialized", {})
        original = await start_thread(2)
        first = await turn(original, 3)
        state["healthy"] = True
        second = await turn(original, 4)
        fresh = await start_thread(5)
        control = await turn(fresh, 6)
        reproduced = first["http_requests"] > 0 and second["ws_requests"] == 0 and second["http_requests"] > 0 and control["ws_requests"] > 0
        print(json.dumps({"client": args.client, "failure_type": args.failure,
                          "initial_failure_then_fallback": first, "next_turn_with_websocket_healthy": second,
                          "fresh_thread_control": control, "sticky_fallback_reproduced": reproduced}, indent=2), flush=True)
        if args.assert_recovery:
            assert second["ws_requests"] > 0 and second["http_requests"] == 0, (
                "RECOVERY_REGRESSION: the existing thread remained on HTTP after WebSockets recovered")
    finally:
        process.stdin.close()
        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(process.wait(), 5)
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            process.kill()
            await process.wait()
        reader.cancel()
        stderr = (await stderr_task).decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        selected = [line for line in stderr.splitlines() if "falling back to HTTP" in line]
        print(json.dumps({"fallback_log": selected[-2:]}), flush=True)
        await runner.cleanup()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

```
</details>

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.description: Issues related to skills

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

ChatGPT/Codex desktop on macOS. Read from the installed app bundle on October 11, 2026:
- Version: `26.1007.30912`
- Build: `20156`
- Bundled CLI: `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2`

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected for this report.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.2 (26B5091g), arm64.

### What issue are you seeing?

**A dot's tasks on a connected Mac do not receive a working local MCP server's tools.** The same server is callable from an ordinary local Codex conversation on that Mac.

The example is [JonathanRReed/Apple-MCPs](https://github.com/JonathanRReed/Apple-MCPs), unified `apple-tools-mcp` v1.1.0, using local stdio transport. This is a tool-exposure problem observed with this server and task path; it has not been established that every local MCP server or every dot is affected.

Two configurations were tested:
1. A global Codex MCP registration named `apple-tools`, enabled and pointing to the installed executable.
2. A local plugin named **Apple Tools Local**, installed and enabled through a local marketplace. Its portable root `plugin.json` and `mcp.json` reference the same executable under a distinct server name, `apple-tools-local`.

Neither configuration exposed Apple tools to the dot-started task.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed sequence on the affected Mac, rather than a clean-install reproduction:

1. Install the Apple-MCPs unified server with `uv tool install apple-tools-mcp==1.1.0`.
2. Register it with `codex mcp add apple-tools -- /ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/apple-tools-mcp`.
3. Confirm that an ordinary local Codex conversation receives the Apple MCP tools. On this machine, actual tool calls succeeded: aggregated health, Reminders list discovery, Mail mailbox discovery and Notes account discovery.
4. Ask the dot to use the installed server on its connected Mac to list Apple Reminders lists through a local task.
5. The task reports that the server is registered locally but absent from its callable tools.
6. Package the same executable as an MCP-only local plugin and install/enable it. The plugin's MCP declaration is:
   ```json
   {
     "$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/mcp.schema.json",
     "mcpServers": {
       "apple-tools-local": {
         "type": "stdio",
         "command": "/ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/apple-tools-mcp",
         "args": []
       }
     }
   }
   ```
7. Ask the dot to use **Apple Tools Local** on the connected Mac to list Reminders lists. The task again reports no callable Apple tools.

A full desktop restart was requested before the plugin retry, but completion of that restart was not independently verified.

### Evidence

Directly verified in the ordinary local environment:
- Global MCP registration: enabled, stdio, installed executable.
- Local plugin: installed and enabled, as reported by `codex plugin list`.
- Launching the installed plugin's declared command through an MCP client passed initialization, tool listing and read-only tool discovery: **184 tools**.
- Real Apple-domain discovery calls succeeded in an ordinary local Codex conversation.

The following is **user-relayed output from the dot's affected task**, not an independently captured backend tool inventory:

> Apple Tools Local still isn't callable, so I couldn't list your Apple Reminders lists.

The task reported these MCP namespaces:
- `mcp__codex_app`
- `mcp__codex_apps`
- `mcp__computer_history`

It also reported separate computer-use and automation tools, but no Apple Reminders tools. It said no Apple personal data was read in the failed dot test.

### What is the expected behavior?

An authorized dot task executing on the connected Mac should be able to discover and call supported, enabled local MCP/plugin tools, as an ordinary local Codex conversation does.

If local stdio MCP servers or local plugins are intentionally unsupported through cloud-coordinated dot work, please state that limitation clearly in the UI and documentation and provide a supported integration route.

Please investigate local MCP/plugin discovery and final tool exposure for dot-started tasks, and clarify which local configuration is honored. The root cause has not been established.

Related symptom: #49458 reports missing Computer Use tools in dot-started Windows tasks despite ordinary local sessions working. This report concerns a custom local stdio MCP on macOS; no shared root cause is asserted.

### Privacy

Local usernames and paths, dot name, account identifiers, task IDs and all Apple personal data are omitted. No raw logs or credentials are included.

## Impact and urgency

User's exact description: **“It's driving the user fucking crazy.”** Repeated notification dings interrupt voice conversations and make remote computer work difficult. The user requests urgent investigation.

## Environment

ChatGPT/Codex desktop app on Windows, coordinating work with another Windows computer through a remote Codex chat. Exact client/build versions have not been captured.

## Steps observed

1. Coordinate a remote chat from a voice conversation.
2. Ask the remote chat to return a short test reply without running tools or deliberately playing sound.
3. Wait for the remote reply to complete.
4. The user hears a ding on their computer.
5. Repeat: several controlled remote-chat replies each produced a ding, according to the user.
6. Disable Codex, Messages, and Responses notifications in the desktop app. The user also reports disabling Windows app notifications on both computers.
7. The user reports that the dings continue.

In one comparison, a local voice-chat test reply did not produce a ding. This suggests a connection to remote completion delivery, but does not establish the exact audio process.

## Expected behavior

Disabling notifications should silence their associated sounds. Provide a separate sound-only mute, per-remote-chat sound control, and an option to change the completion sound, while preserving voice audio and visual alerts.

## Actual behavior

Remote-chat completion dings continued after the reported notification settings were disabled. No sound-only or per-remote-chat mute control was visible in the supplied settings screenshot.

## Diagnostic limitations

The exact audio process, underlying sound event, and app version remain unverified. Windows Volume Mixer did not display an explicitly named ChatGPT/Codex entry at the time inspected. No private chat contents, logs, screenshots, account identifiers, or business details are included in this report.

items.title: [Windows 11] ChatGPT/Codex MSIX installation repeatedly fails with 0x80073CF6 / 0x80070005 – stale packaged service registration

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1007.2314.0

### What subscription do you have?

plus

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Home Single Language (Chinese), x64, Build 26200.9457

### What issue are you seeing?

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 Home Single Language (Chinese), x64
- Windows build: 26200.9457
- Installation source: Microsoft Store
- Package family: `OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0`
- Current staged package: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1007.2314.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0`
- Previously installed version referenced by the Windows service: `26.928.3736.0`

## Issue description

The ChatGPT/Codex Windows desktop application repeatedly fails to install or update through Microsoft Store.

After restarting Windows, the application may become unavailable through its normal Windows entry points, even though its executable files remain under `C:\Program Files\WindowsApps`.

The executable can sometimes be launched directly, but Windows fails to register the application package correctly.

The problem has occurred repeatedly since October 9, 2026.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install or update the ChatGPT/Codex desktop application using Microsoft Store.
2. Restart Windows or retry application installation/registration.
3. Windows attempts to register the `OpenAI.Codex` MSIX package.
4. Registration fails during the `windows.service` extension registration phase.
5. The package remains in the `Servicing` / `Staged` state.
6. Subsequent installation or registration attempts fail with the same errors.

## Expected behavior

The ChatGPT/Codex desktop application should install and update successfully through Microsoft Store.

Application package registration should complete without requiring repeated reinstalls or manual intervention.

## Actual behavior

The package is staged, but Windows fails to register its packaged service extension.

The following PowerShell command:

`Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers -Name OpenAI.Codex`

returns:

```
Name                   : OpenAI.Codex
Version                : 26.1007.2314.0
Status                 : Servicing
PackageUserInformation : {S-1-5-18 [S-1-5-18]: Staged}
```

## Relevant Windows event logs

Source: `Microsoft-Windows-AppXDeploymentServer/Operational`

**October 11, 2026, 22:13:57 — Event ID 306**

```
Error 0x80070005:
Windows could not register the windows.service extension.
Access is denied.
```

**October 11, 2026, 22:13:57 — Event ID 316**

```
Error 0x80070005:
The registration request failed because access was denied
while registering the windows.service extension.
```

**October 11, 2026, 22:13:57 — Event ID 331**

```
Error 0x8007139F:
The group or resource is not in the correct state
to perform the requested operation.
```

**October 11, 2026, 22:13:57 — Event ID 300**

```
Error 0x80073CF6:
Unable to register package OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0.
Package registration failed.
```

**October 11, 2026, 22:13:58 — Event ID 404**

```
AppX deployment of package
OpenAI.Codex_26.1007.2314.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0
failed with error 0x80073CF6.

Underlying error:
0x80070005 — Access denied during
windows.service extension registration.
```

**October 11, 2026, 22:13:58 — Event ID 649**

```
ACLs repaired successfully for
C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\
OpenAI.Codex_26.1007.2314.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0.

Register next time should succeed.
```

However, subsequent registration attempts continue to fail.

**Additional error — October 11, 2026, 20:58:55 — Event ID 404**

```
Error 0x80073D28:
Administrator privileges are required
to install a packaged service.
```

The `0x80070005` failure also occurs when attempting package registration from an elevated administrator PowerShell session.

## Possible stale packaged service

Windows still contains the following service:

`CodexSandboxService.OpenAI.Codex`

Observed service details:

```
Service name: CodexSandboxService.OpenAI.Codex
Display name: ChatGPT
Status: Stopped
Start type: Manual
```

The service's registered executable path points to the previous package:

```
C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\
OpenAI.Codex_26.928.3736.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0\
app\resources\codex-windows-sandbox-service.exe
```

However:

- The old executable path no longer exists (`Test-Path` returns `False`).
- The new version's sandbox service executable exists (`Test-Path` returns `True`).
- `Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers` only reports the newer package.
- Attempting to delete the old service using elevated PowerShell returns `OpenService FAILED 5: Access is denied`.

This suggests that a stale packaged service registration may be involved, although the root cause has not been confirmed.

## Troubleshooting already attempted

- Reinstalled the application through Microsoft Store.
- Restarted Windows multiple times.
- Used `Add-AppxPackage -RegisterByFamilyName` to register the staged package.
- Retried registration using `-ForceApplicationShutdown`.
- Ran `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` successfully.
- Ran `sfc /scannow`, which found and successfully repaired corrupted system files.
- Confirmed that AppXSvc, ClipSVC, InstallService and StateRepository were running.
- Confirmed elevated administrator privileges.
- Inspected the packaged service registration and associated executable paths.

The error persists after all these steps.

I have not performed a forced deletion of the service registry key or a full all-users/provisioned-package removal.

## Questions for the maintainers

1. Could the stale `CodexSandboxService.OpenAI.Codex` registration prevent subsequent MSIX package versions from registering their packaged services?
2. Is there a supported way to repair this service registration without modifying protected Windows service permissions?
3. Could the installer/update process detect and recover from an existing packaged service pointing to a removed application version?
4. Is there a recommended recovery method that preserves local Codex data, sessions and Skills?

I would appreciate any guidance or an installer-side fix, as this issue currently prevents reliable daily use of the Windows desktop application.

Thank you!




### What steps can reproduce the bug?

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use Windows 11 Home Single Language (Chinese), x64, build 26200.9457.
2. Install or update the ChatGPT/Codex Windows desktop application through Microsoft Store.
3. Restart Windows or attempt to launch the application after an update.
4. The installation or update process fails, and the application may disappear from the Start menu or become unavailable through its normal launch entry.
5. The new application files remain in `C:\Program Files\WindowsApps`, and the executable can sometimes be launched manually.
6. Open PowerShell and run:

   `Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers -Name OpenAI.Codex`

   The package is reported as `Servicing`, with `PackageUserInformation` showing `Staged`.

7. Attempt to register the existing package from an elevated PowerShell session:

   `Add-AppxPackage -RegisterByFamilyName -MainPackage "OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0" -ForceApplicationShutdown`

8. The registration fails with `0x80073CF6`. The underlying error is `0x80070005: Access denied` while registering the `windows.service` extension.

9. In Windows Event Viewer, navigate to:

   `Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > Windows > AppXDeploymentServer > Operational`

   Events 306, 316, 331, 300 and 404 record the service registration and package deployment failures.

### Reproducibility

The problem has occurred repeatedly across multiple installation and update attempts since October 9, 2026. Restarting Windows and repairing system components with DISM and SFC did not resolve it.

### What is the expected behavior?

_No response_

### Additional information

### Possibly related issue

This issue may be related to #38843, which reports repeated MSIX auto-update failures on Windows.

However, my case specifically involves `0x80070005` during `windows.service` extension registration, along with a packaged sandbox service still pointing to an older, no longer existing application version.

I am filing this report separately to provide the detailed Windows deployment logs and service registration findings.

In the ChatGPT Android app, when Codex presents an interactive multiple-choice question and the user selects "Other" to provide a custom response, the Android keyboard covers the text input field, preventing the user from seeing what they are typing.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open a Codex session in the ChatGPT Android app.
2. Have Codex present an interactive question with multiple-choice options and an "Other" option.
3. Select "Other".
4. Tap the custom text input field.
5. The Android keyboard appears and obscures the input field.

Expected behavior:
The question interface should automatically resize, reposition, or scroll to keep the focused input field visible above the keyboard.

Actual behavior:
The keyboard overlays the input field, hiding the text being entered.

Environment:
- Platform: Android
- Application: ChatGPT Android app, Codex integration
- Affected component: Interactive question "Other" input
- Normal ChatGPT message entry works correctly.

Suspected cause:
The interactive question component may not correctly handle Android IME window insets or focus-driven scrolling.

Potential fixes:
- Handle WindowInsets.ime / WindowInsetsCompat correctly.
- Resize or reposition the question dialog when the keyboard appears.
- Automatically scroll the focused text field into view.

- Reading installed Windows app package metadata with Get-AppxPackage was denied; no escalation or settings change was performed.

Please identify the failed known-folder identifier and launcher context in supported diagnostics, provide a supported recovery for the browser launcher, and clarify the supported setup that exposes official Windows full-desktop Computer Use when its package is installed but the task lacks node_repl and native APIs are disabled. items.title: [macOS] Existing tool/image chats fail after HTTP 200 across two app builds; same-core minimal probe succeeds

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Verified from the installed macOS app bundle:
- Initial failures: 26.1007.21159 (build 20052)
- Failures after the app update/restart: 26.1007.30912 (build 20156)

The bundled core is `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2` in both observations. The current core version was also checked by running the bundled binary with `--version`.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro (the affected Responses request headers reported `x-codex-plan-type: pro`; no raw headers are attached).

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple silicon / arm64. Local execution in the ChatGPT-branded desktop app (Codex runtime).

### What issue are you seeing?

Two independent existing local conversations, one involving image composition and one involving presentation review/editing, repeatedly fail to continue. The UI reaches “Reconnecting 5/5” and reports:

```text
stream disconnected before completion: An error occurred while processing your request. You can retry your request, or contact us through our help center at help.openai.com if the error persists. Please include the request ID ... in your message.
```

This is an observed reliability failure, not a claim that the root cause is proven.

The same endpoint/model is involved: `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`, `gpt-6.1-sol`, reasoning effort `xhigh`.

#### Correlated failures on 2026-10-11 (UTC+8)

| Workflow | Time | Terminal request ID |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Image workflow, initial build | 21:34:32 | 2e1292ce-f47d-48a2-b3a9-1a7cf263c91b |
| Image workflow, initial build | 21:46:57 | 83276a4d-b18b-4e04-bd7c-66b72399f41c |
| Presentation workflow, updated build | 22:09:29 | b2f45aa4-0fcb-4f21-a4e3-3d5d291b84f6 |
| Image workflow, updated build | 22:12:35 | d056e4c5-7dba-4d31-98e6-68d0d55c5daa |

Affected local session IDs:
- Image workflow: `01a12ad0-63a0-70b2-b1c1-e0b3933cf5cd`
- Presentation workflow: `01a12af9-a295-7b91-8c0c-4e5f2c6e98ea`

The presentation terminal turn is `01a12b49-5beb-79b1-8e9c-804c60764110`; the post-update image terminal turn is `01a12b49-5bc9-77a1-b54b-57d725fde0be`.

#### Exact transport observations after the update

For the presentation failure:
1. 22:06:45–22:07:16: five retries report `websocket closed by server before response.completed`.
2. 22:07:28: `codex_core::client` logs `falling back to HTTP`.
3. Five further HTTP attempts report the generic processing error above.
4. The final `codex_http_client::client` record at 22:09:28 has `status=200 OK`, `version=HTTP/1.1`, the Responses endpoint, and `x-oai-request-id=b2f45aa4-0fcb-4f21-a4e3-3d5d291b84f6`.
5. The next terminal turn record at 22:09:29 reports that exact request ID and the processing error.

The post-update image continuation also encountered `Broken pipe (os error 32)` and a WebSocket close, fell back to HTTP at 22:09:07, then failed after HTTP processing-error retries.

HTTP 200 here confirms received response headers, **not** a completed response stream. The raw SSE error event was not captured, so the precise upstream error code is unknown. Please correlate the request IDs server-side.

#### Request size / context comparison

- Presentation failure: raw request body 18,808,335 bytes; zstd-compressed body about 13,708,670 bytes.
- Initial image failures: compressed request bodies grew from about 39.4 MB to 54.2 MB (decimal MB).
- Both histories contain a recorded context-compaction event before these failures.
- Image history's last recorded successful model input before the initial failures was about 249,726 tokens against a reported 760,000-token context window.
- The latest inspected presentation input record was about 302,676 tokens against the same reported window, but it belongs to the subsequently resumed work, **not necessarily the exact failed request**.

These observations do not establish a context-size threshold or a text-context overflow. In particular, the smaller presentation request also failed, so the largest image payload cannot by itself explain all incidents.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed sequence (intermittent; no public deterministic reproducer yet):

1. Work in an existing local desktop conversation with multiple tool calls and inspected/rendered images.
2. Complete and save a meaningful artifact.
3. Send a short follow-up requesting continuation or a text deliverable based on the saved artifact.
4. Observe retries, WebSocket-to-HTTP fallback on the updated build, and terminal processing-error failure.
5. Repeating continuation after the app update/restart can fail in both independent histories.

Redacted examples of the follow-up requests:
- “Has the image generation finished?”
- “Write a roughly ten-minute narration based on the saved presentation.”
- “Continue.”

**Same-machine minimal control, actually executed:** using the currently bundled core, the existing user configuration, the same model and reasoning effort, and the current network:

```sh
<bundled-codex> exec --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --json --color never \
  --sandbox read-only --model gpt-6.1-sol \
  -c 'model_reasoning_effort="xhigh"' \
  'Diagnostic connectivity probe only. Reply with exactly STREAM_PROBE_OK. Do not use tools, read files, run commands, or modify anything.'
```

The probe returned `STREAM_PROBE_OK` and a `turn.completed` event (34,827 input tokens; 8 output tokens). The contemporaneous diagnostic desktop conversation also continued without response-retry warnings.

This single successful control does not rule out intermittent network faults or reproduce the larger existing conversation's input. It does show that the same core/account/model/network is not failing on every request.

### What is the expected behavior?

Existing conversations should remain continuable, with completed files/actions preserved. When a stream fails, please expose an actionable failure classification and provide a supported in-place recovery path. A generic “Reconnecting” label should not obscure the distinction between a transport interruption and an upstream processing failure.

### Additional information

Read-only local checks found no custom model-provider/base-URL override, no per-project Codex configuration override in the two affected workspaces, and no HTTP/HTTPS/ALL_PROXY environment variables in the diagnostic process. At inspection time macOS explicit HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS/PAC proxy settings were disabled. A VPN client/core process was running; its historical traffic path was **not** reconstructed, and no controlled alternative-network test was performed. Network involvement is therefore not completely excluded.

No local network/model/global configuration was changed, no application files were patched, and the affected conversations were not replayed by the diagnostic probe. The presentation conversation had already been resumed by the user; this investigation did not send messages or repeat external actions in it.

Completed image files survived the failed turns and were independently verified. This matters because retries of a task can risk repeating already-completed external actions.

Requested investigation:
1. Correlate the four request IDs and determine the actual upstream processing-error code and failing component.
2. Determine whether existing multimodal/tool conversation state, the shared core version, or WebSocket/HTTP recovery contributes.
3. Identify a supported recovery/workaround that preserves existing history and work; clarify whether a core/app fix or backend remediation is required.
4. Improve error reporting so transport failures and semantic processing errors are distinguishable.

I searched existing reports. Possibly related: #52814 and #52731. They share symptoms; a shared root cause is not established. This report adds cross-workflow/cross-build evidence, precise HTTP/request-ID correlation, smaller-payload failure, and an executed same-core control. Please consolidate if appropriate.

No screenshots, business documents, personal photos, raw transcripts, raw response headers, auth credentials, account email addresses, or local usernames/paths are included.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os

labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

items.body:
### Summary
On Windows, both the Codex Desktop integrated browser controller and native computer-use Node runtime exit before initialization with:
`MXC launcher: enumerate MXC volume D:\\: The volume does not contain a recognized file system. (os error 1005)`

This follows the unrelated-volume enumeration cases in #51686 and #50915. The additional observation is that an officially configured narrow permission profile permits a forced-MXC CLI probe on the same host, but the computer/browser controllers still return the unrelated-volume error after selecting Custom permissions and restarting the desktop app.

### Verified versions
- Desktop About/update report: 26.1007.21434, production, up to date when checked.
- Installed Windows package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.2314.0.
- Desktop-managed Codex core: 0.162.0-alpha.17.2.
- Bundled CUA archive: cua-node-0.0.29-20261005054403-144090e2ddcb-windows-x64.

### Narrow-profile comparison
A named profile was configured through the documented permissions system, without `:root`, without inheritance from `:workspace`, with `:minimal` read, workspace writes, protected .git/.codex/.agents/.aws reads, narrow runtime read grants, and network disabled. No approval policy was weakened.

Using the exact desktop-managed codex.exe:
- `codex sandbox -P controller-repair -c 'windows.sandbox="mxc"' ... powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command 'Write-Output "...verification marker..."'` printed the marker and exited 0.
- Repeating with the exact bundled pwsh.exe, after granting its runtime directory read access, also printed the marker and exited 0.
- After selecting Custom (config.toml), the conversation's effective filesystem description changed from `:root` to `:minimal` plus the scoped grants.
- Resetting the official CUA JavaScript kernel and calling `await cua.getState()` still exited 1 with D: enumeration error 1005, before obtaining page/app inventory.
- The official native computer-use Node initialization failed with the same error.

The CLI probes are not proof that the integrated tools used the same launch policy. Full internal launcher payloads are not available. Please investigate how their effective sandbox policy differs.

### Backend fallback already tested and reverted
A specifically authorized temporary managed policy disallowing MXC was tested. The CUA tool rejected it because it explicitly selected Mxc; it did not fall back to elevated. The introduced policy was then removed and absence verified. No sandbox was disabled.

### Expected behavior
Official browser/computer controllers should honor a supported scoped filesystem permission profile, or document the required runtime grants, without enumerating unrelated volumes. Automatically generated inaccessible volume roots should not block initialization; explicit inaccessible-path requests should remain fail-closed.

### Scope and limitations
No disk contents were inspected. No formatting, filesystem repair, unmounting, drive-letter removal, partition changes, security-feature disabling, credential extraction, or runtime/package patching was performed. The D: filesystem type has not been established, and error 1005 alone is not proof of corruption. A runtime/core change coincided with the failure, but causality has not been proven.

This report omits usernames, private project paths, chat identifiers, credentials, tokens, and full private logs.

### Additional isolation probe
The exact bundled node.exe (v24.21.0) was launched through the exact desktop-managed `codex sandbox` with the restricted named profile and explicitly forced MXC. A single `console.log` marker printed and the process exited 0; no UI, browser service, network request, or Node REPL kernel was initialized. This establishes that the official Node executable can launch inside MXC with this scoped policy, while the integrated controllers fail with volume enumeration error 1005.

Read-only inspection of static strings in the bundled node_repl.exe also found explicit `windows.sandbox="mxc"` and generated permission-selection strings. This is not a capture of its complete launch payload. No executable, plugin file, environment transport, or internal security setting was patched.

### Verified local recovery
A subsequent full desktop relaunch with Custom (config.toml) already selected recovered the integrated controller on this host. The effective profile includes :minimal and narrow runtime/workspace grants, with no :root grant. `cua.getState()` returned the browser inventory, and creating/reading an about:blank tab succeeded. Initially, external navigation was denied because networking was deliberately disabled in this diagnostic profile. After explicit user approval, a proxy-backed allowlist for one public project domain was configured. The controller then loaded that page, read its accessibility state, and clicked a FAQ button; the expanded answer was verified. No drive state or security protections were changed.

This is a verified local workaround, not an upstream fix or an isolated proof of which restart/configuration step was causal. Native computer-use was not independently rechecked. The earlier failed probes remain part of the report so others can distinguish the before/after sequence.

items.title: [Windows desktop] Repeated sign-in-screen/session-loss incidents on 26.1002/26.1007; stable after rollback to 26.930

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Affected Windows package versions observed in local desktop logs:
- `OpenAI.Codex 26.1002.7124.0`
- `OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.2314.0`

Rolled back to `OpenAI.Codex 26.930.7945.0`. The running app's update-check tool reports app version `26.930.61225`, build `13232`, production channel. These are different version fields, not conflicting package versions.

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected for this report.

### What platform is your computer?

- Windows 11 Pro 25H2, build `26200.9457`, x64.
- NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 SUPER, driver `32.0.16.1047`.
- Approximately 32 GB RAM.
- The machine is also accessed remotely using Windows Remote Desktop and AweSun. Several virtual display adapters are installed. No causal role for remote access or those drivers has been established.

### What issue are you seeing?

During October 9–10, 2026, while using the newer Codex desktop releases, I repeatedly found the computer back at the Windows PIN/sign-in screen. After signing in, the programs from the previous session were closed. The behavior looked like an unexpected sign-out or a system restart, rather than just the Codex window closing.

After rolling back to `26.930.7945.0` on October 10, I have not observed another such incident through the evening of October 11. This suggests a possible desktop regression or interaction with this machine's Windows/driver environment; it does **not** prove a specific Codex component is the cause.

There had been occasional unexplained restart events before these updates. The notable change was the reported increase in frequency on October 9–10, followed by the stable observation period after rollback. This was normal usage, not a controlled reproduction with every other variable held fixed.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

I do not yet have a deterministic minimal reproduction. The observed sequence was:

1. Use the Windows desktop application during the period with the newer package versions.
2. Experience repeated returns to the Windows sign-in screen with the previous session's applications closed. Some incidents were noticed through remote access or while the machine was unattended.
3. Roll back the app to `26.930.7945.0`.
4. Continue using the machine; the reported symptom has not recurred during the subsequent observation period.

I have not reinstalled the affected release just to reproduce possible session/data loss.

The version timeline below is independently recorded in local desktop logs. All times are **Asia/Shanghai, UTC+08:00**:

| Time | Observed desktop startup |
| --- | --- |
| 2026-10-09 10:40:41 | Package `26.1002.7124.0` |
| 2026-10-10 08:05:39 | Package `26.1007.2314.0` |
| 2026-10-10 14:58:42 | Rolled-back package `26.930.7945.0` |

### What is the expected behavior?

Using or leaving the Codex desktop app open should not unexpectedly end the Windows session or destabilize the operating system. A failure in the app or one of its helpers should be diagnosable without losing other applications in the session.

Please investigate whether there is a known regression affecting these builds, identify any released fix, and advise which supported diagnostics would distinguish a session termination from a kernel/driver failure.

### Additional information

A read-only review of Windows events and the desktop logs found:

- Seven `Kernel-Power 41` / `EventLog 6008` pairs with corresponding `Kernel-General 12` startups during October 9–10. All seven event 41 records had `BugcheckCode=0`. **These are not being presented as seven Codex-caused failures**: some restarts were deliberate, and not every logged restart has been matched to the symptom. Event 41 is recorded at the next startup and does not identify the original cause. I also recall incidents for which I did not find an obvious corresponding log entry; exact incident-to-event matching remains incomplete.
- The deliberate AweSun restart on October 9 at 16:13 was confirmed separately. Another restart at 17:22 was explicitly requested by Windows Defender while remediating a TrafficMonitor WinRing0 driver. Those should not be conflated with the unexplained incidents.
- TrafficMonitor was removed later on October 9, but another unexplained startup was reported on October 10 before the Codex rollback. Its removal did not by itself end the reported problem.
- Available Winlogon/session-manager sign-out records coincide with recorded system shutdown sequences. No separate abnormal sign-out cause has been identified. Windows Security auditing and protected kernel-dump directories were not accessible to this diagnostic session; absence of a usable dump in this report does not establish absence of a system crash.
- Some desktop logs stop abruptly before later system startups, without an explicit app crash or normal-exit marker. The reviewed logs did not show a clear GPU/OOM/renderer-crash signature. Abrupt truncation alone does not establish causation.
- There is no local crash stack establishing which module failed. No power, driver, BIOS, sandbox, or security settings were changed during this investigation.

Potentially related reports, **not confirmed duplicates**:

runtime read/execute validation failed:

The Chinese message means that another program is using the file and the process cannot access it.

items.title: Proposal: Gary's 4tope for dependency-aware chat continuity and inference context

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: context
labels.description: Issues related to context management (including compaction)

items.body:
## Feature proposal: dependency-aware chat continuity

I am offering **Gary's 4tope**, framed and named by **Gary Stimpson on 2026-10-10**, as an experiment for Codex's context-retention policy. I am using the issue channel in accordance with the current contribution guide. The reviewable proposal is [draft PR #2 in my Codex fork](https://github.com/gary23w/codex/pull/2), with a [detailed design and pinned source map](https://github.com/gary23w/codex/blob/1e1e41000e4bc9b833203aa550654dfdce45d767/docs/proposals/gary-4tope-context-geometry.md) and an [offline Rust reference](https://github.com/gary23w/codex/blob/1e1e41000e4bc9b833203aa550654dfdce45d767/docs/proposals/gary-4tope/reference.rs).

This is an offer for maintainer-led evaluation, not an external upstream code PR or a claim that production Codex already implements the design.

## User problem and desired behavior

A long chat can reach a context boundary after reading a specification, trying an unsuccessful approach, editing a file and verifying the fix. Its next inference needs the actual prerequisites of that work: the old specification, exact identifiers and tool observations, the user's constraints, relevant failures and current next action. Recency and dependency relevance are different quantities.

For example, “keep MAGIC_V2 and do not deploy” must survive even if the agent's latest text does not repeat those words. An unrelated recent configuration read should not crowd out the parser evidence the current edit depends on. A new successful test result should be distinguished from an older failure, with the workspace revision attached.

The desired behavior is a bounded, source-backed continuation that carries the evidence nearest the current work, preserves obligations independently of lexical reuse, and makes omissions and fallback explicit.

## Natural geometry, precisely

Gary's organizing analogy is the net of a 4-polytope: a connected object needs an unfolding before it can be read as a flat view. Here work events are nodes, dependencies are adjacency, and a tree determines presentation. This is graph geometry, not a claim that chats have literal 4D coordinates or that model attention is being replaced.

The [original implementation in NL-Veil](https://github.com/gary23w/nl-veil/blob/a6b1b5d8c6e3a667e8d7436667b17ab16265fbda/src/worker/chat/net.zig) separates protection, retrieval and layout.

## The formula

Let G=(V,E) be the working-span DAG. Every dependency v→u points to an older event u; f is the frontier assistant step.

**Protection** uses the longest weighted dependency path:

```text
L(v) = max(0, max{ L(u) + w(v,u) : u in deps(v) })
L(v) = 0 when deps(v) is empty
```

Compute oldest first, record the maximizing predecessor, then follow predecessors from f. The original weights are 2 for detected reuse of a previous-round result, 1 for issuing-step/thread links, and 0 for a previous-round observation with no detected reuse. Live results on that chain are protected from the original pruning pass. Equal positive scores favor the newer dependency.

For issuer s0, result r1 and consuming step s2, the backward path s2→r1→s0 scores 3, while the direct thread edge s2→s0 scores 1. This is O(V+E) dynamic programming on the DAG.

**Retrieval** traverses each dependency in both directions:

```text
c(a,b) = c0(a,b) + 4*I[b superseded] + I[b failed]
d(f) = 0
d(v) = minimum total c along a path from f to v
```

I is the indicator function. c0 is 1 for used/issued/thread edges and 3 for weak observation edges. Dijkstra computes distances and predecessors. Costs include destination penalties, so opposite traversal directions can have different costs.

Admit optional observations in increasing d, newer first on ties, when they fit the remaining budget. A shortest-path tree controls a deterministic depth-first layout. NEXT is the frontier, ON DISK is verified engine state, RULED OUT is state-dependent failure evidence, and ESTABLISHED is retained observations. This greedy rule is inspectable; it is not claimed to be an optimal knapsack solution.

**Important qualification:** a longest path is one chain, not the full prerequisite closure. Two essential branches require a separate must-keep policy or multiple protected chains. Original lexical-overlap detection is a heuristic, and original user nodes are not automatically included in the unfolding. The reference adds caller-pinned obligations and explicit oversized-mandatory fallback.

## Where it fits in current Codex

Analysis is pinned to upstream [a07c8ebd57feedc4cf5dfe854c8e9101de54186b](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/a07c8ebd57feedc4cf5dfe854c8e9101de54186b).

- Build a bounded graph from typed `ResponseItemEnvelope` events in `context_manager/history.rs`, before destructive clipping, preserving original roles and host provenance.
- Evaluate dependency protection before `compact_remote_history.rs` rewrites outputs; preserve tool-call/output groups and notices.
- Compare graph ranking with the newest-first retained-message policy in `compact_remote_v2.rs`. Initially keep the opaque remote compaction item and existing canonical context.
- The clearest later local-carry seam is `Session::start_new_context_window`, used by `compact_token_budget.rs`. **Codex already has a no-summary token-budget path**; avoiding a summarizer call alone is not the novel contribution.
- Preserve the existing replacement/rollout lifecycle, completeness metadata, user-authorization boundaries and `context_manager/normalize.rs` pairing rules.
- Route experiments through the capability-aware compaction branches in `session/turn.rs`, rather than patching only local `compact.rs`.

The full proposal links each seam to its inspected source and distinguishes its newer upstream analysis from the fork's existing base. This concerns the public harness's inference inputs; it does not assert access to weights, hidden reasoning or serving internals.

## Why it is a promising chat design

The architectural benefit is that source identity, execution state and explicit dependencies can be handled deterministically. Old relevant evidence can outrank recent noise; retained identifiers need not be paraphrased; failures can remain visible; selected evidence can be traced to its source.

The candidate quality improvements are fewer redundant reads, fewer inappropriate repeats of unsuccessful calls, and more accurate continuation at matched context budgets. These remain hypotheses for model-backed evaluation. Source selection is lossy. A tree does not make every original graph path simultaneously contiguous. Model compaction may still be valuable for implicit reasoning, semantic synthesis, visual content and ambiguous tasks.

Production adaptations include full-argument/state-aware supersession, exact UTF-8 spans, tool-observation provenance, required-branch completeness, real provider-token/image accounting, cache effects, snapshot-version checks and atomic fallback. A failed newer read must not erase an earlier success just because the path matches.

## Evidence and proposed next step

The Rust mathematical reference passed **12 offline tests** with rustc 1.96.0 on Windows, including weighted chains, asymmetric distance, stale filtering, pinned disconnected obligations, failures, every budget from 0 through 1399, Unicode, cycles, oversized optional evidence, deterministic layout, 100-child fanout and the single-chain limitation.

It is not wired into Codex and does not implement production dependency extraction, protocol serialization, tokenization or durable storage. No full Codex build or comparative model-backed benchmark was run. [NL-Veil's release evidence](https://github.com/gary23w/nl-veil/blob/a6b1b5d8c6e3a667e8d7436667b17ab16265fbda/docs/release/RELEASE-v1.1.16.md) reports scripted end-to-end continuation while explicitly leaving hosted-model long-task continuation unverified.

A useful first step would be default-off shadow selection against the existing remote/local and token-budget paths, followed by a retention-only experiment. Measure prerequisite recall, exact-value retention, user-constraint preservation, stale-state errors, repeated calls, completion quality, total/cached tokens, re-reads and p95 latency at matched total budgets. Ablate dependency detection, chain protection, distance, failure handling and layout separately.

Maintainer feedback on the retention seam and representative replay workloads would help determine whether this approach merits an internal prototype.

items.body:
## Summary

Chrome Browser Use in the Windows desktop app repeatedly fails with:

```text
Unable to load browser request-header policy. Retry the browser command.
```

The documented browser-selection call succeeds and returns Chrome documentation, but subsequent browser operations fail before any page content is returned. Resetting the CUA JavaScript kernel and initializing the same connected browser again does not resolve the failure.

## Environment

- Observed: October 11, 2026 (Asia/Jerusalem).
- Windows 11; previously collected OS build: 10.0.26200.
- Installed app version: `26.1007.21434`.
- Build: `13901`, production channel.
- Built-in app update checker reports `up_to_date`.
- Browser: Google Chrome through the extension provider.
- Tool: `mcp__cua_repl`.
- Current Windows sandbox configuration: `unelevated`.
- Chrome and extension versions and subscription: not collected.

## Reproduction

1. Select the connected Chrome provider using the documented `cua.getBrowser` API. This succeeds and returns browser documentation.
2. Run the documented browser task operations: `nameSession`, `tabs.new`, `goto` to a public Google Search URL, and `playwright.domSnapshot`.
3. The tool returns the request-header policy error above; no page snapshot is returned.
4. Retry through `cua.createBrowserTab` with a session name and the same public search destination: the same error occurs.
5. Reset the CUA JavaScript kernel with `mcp__cua_repl.js_reset`, select Chrome again, and retry the documented task operations.
6. The same failure occurs. A later retry in the same chat also fails.

The sequential task operations were submitted together, so the precise first failing operation within that sequence has not been independently identified.

## Read-only diagnostic findings

- Local shell execution currently succeeds. The earlier Windows sandbox startup error is not reproduced by current shell checks.
- The installed browser service contains this exact error in the function that waits for Statsig initialization/readiness before reading a browser request-header feature gate.
- That function rejects if the awaited readiness result is unsuccessful or the client loading status is not `Ready`.
- The installed browser service configures its Statsig endpoint as `https://ab.chatgpt.com/v1`.
- DNS resolution for `ab.chatgpt.com` succeeds.
- An unauthenticated host-side HTTPS HEAD probe to `/v1/initialize` reaches the server and receives HTTP 403. This is only connectivity evidence: HEAD without SDK credentials is not equivalent to the actual SDK request and does not establish that 403 causes the browser failure.
- A separate sandboxed curl probe fails through its configured local proxy. The browser service's actual fetch transport was not traced, so this is not proof that the same network restriction causes the browser failure.

## Previous, distinct failure

An earlier app version produced `setup refresh had errors` with Windows error 32 while validating `node_repl.exe`. Switching to the documented `unelevated` fallback restored browser access at that time. The current failure is a different error, persists in `unelevated`, and occurs while the browser service is loading request-header policy.

## Expected behavior

The browser service should load the required policy and permit authorized browser tasks. If policy initialization cannot complete, it should expose actionable diagnostics and a supported recovery procedure while preserving security checks.

## Impact and limits

Browser page reads and navigation tasks are blocked. This latest failure has been reproduced in the existing chat after a CUA kernel reset; reproduction in a completely new chat has not yet been tested.

No browser policy checks were patched or bypassed. No private transcripts, website content, email addresses, credentials, cookies, personal paths, session IDs, or screenshots are attached. The user explicitly requested reporting this issue.

Potentially related symptom: #53062 reports the same request-header policy error on the in-app browser on macOS. This report concerns Windows Chrome extension control and does not claim a shared root cause.

## Reliability / model-quality failure report

The user explicitly asked to report this as an **Astra Ultra failure**. The selected model/effort is user-reported; this report does not independently establish an underlying model-service defect.

**Environment:** Codex desktop on Windows, app version 26.1007.2314.0, multi-agent coding workflow, AMD Vivado 2025.2. Observed on 11 October 2026. Private project source, credentials, licenses and proprietary assets are omitted.

### Observed failures

1. Agent-authored FPGA audit logic admitted only one form of a generated alias name. A native diagnostic later encountered another actual optimized alias and stopped before the remaining capacity/ownership checks.
2. The corrected successor still rejected all 16 replay scopes during boundary discovery: a parent synchronous-set register (FDSE) was excluded by an FDRE-only model, and an optimized permission driver was outside the assumed hierarchy. The checker had not exported the complete graph required to model these cases before attempting the next qualification.
3. Independent capacity checks were sequenced after a source proof that stopped on its first failing driver. This withheld downstream evidence and forced another expensive checkpoint load. One measured checkpoint reload took 6 minutes 39 seconds; the failed successor ran approximately 9 minutes.
4. An independent board's repeated recovery/admission failures occurred before placement, yielding no new physical timing. Preparation of its corrected continuation lagged behind a known failure. The replacement was finally dispatched at 15:03 SAST.
5. A 15:15 target for the other replacement launch was missed. After explicit user steering to run a provisional candidate while diagnostics continued, that build launched at 15:26 SAST. Its qualification remains incomplete.

### Impact

The user reports extensive lost development time over repeated long build attempts and substantial paid AI allowance spent correcting agent-introduced defects. Exact usage attributable to these errors has not been measured. No timing-accepted bitstream was produced during the observed period.

### Expected behavior

- Examine complete optimized topology and all affected failure classes before claiming a repair is ready.
- Collect independent evidence even when another check fails, retaining truthful per-phase status.
- Reuse unchanged, source-bound completed evidence instead of repeating expensive work.
- Prepare recoveries promptly once the required evidence is available.
- Clearly distinguish dispatched workers, preflight success, implementation progress and timing acceptance.
- Follow authorized parallel-build instructions without unnecessary serial blocking.

items.body:
# Native source selection for encrypted V2 child tasks before their first response

## What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex Desktop with bundled `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2` and MultiAgent V2.
Source observations below refer to upstream tag `rust-v0.162.0-alpha.17.2`,
commit `740e5af33c71225640e0c1c1555c514c2c93ab74`.

## What feature would you like to see?

An opt-in native phase that automatically selects authorized optional sources
for a child task before its first model response, without requiring either
agent to call a selector helper or generate routing metadata manually.

The use case is an external advisory selector such as Jev, evaluating only a
bounded public task summary and descriptions from the child's effective skill
catalog. The selected model, reasoning effort, profile, permissions, mandatory
readings, and encrypted task body must remain unchanged.

This needs two supported capabilities:

1. A platform-produced, authorized public task summary that is bound to the
   native child task identity and remains separate from its encrypted body.
   The summary must be generated automatically, not delegated to the parent.
2. A native pre-response selector phase that waits for one bounded attempt,
   records the actual outcome in runtime state, and supplies permitted source
   references to the child. Duplicate delivery and repeated helper requests
   should reuse the outcome, including after failure or timeout.

When external processing is disallowed or no safe authorized summary exists,
record an explicit skipped outcome and continue with local sources. The feature
must not export the full task, conversation, private bodies, credentials,
local paths, or ciphertext. Network access alone is not export authorization.

## Additional information

The local prerequisite gap in the checked upstream version is reproducible
from source:

- [V2 message classification](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/740e5af33c71225640e0c1c1555c514c2c93ab74/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_v2.rs#L54):
  ordinary tool-originated messages become `AgentMessage::Encrypted`; only
  `DirectPlaintextMessage` uses the plaintext variant.
- [Communication construction and model input](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/740e5af33c71225640e0c1c1555c514c2c93ab74/codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs#L820):
  `new_encrypted` leaves `content` empty; `to_model_input_item` forwards the
  opaque payload as `AgentMessageInputContent::EncryptedContent`.
- [Input hook dispatch](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/740e5af33c71225640e0c1c1555c514c2c93ab74/codex-rs/core/src/hook_runtime.rs#L677):
  `UserPromptSubmit` handles `UserInput`, while `InterAgentCommunication`
  returns no hook context.
- The existing upstream test
  `multi_agent_v2_spawn_returns_path_and_send_message_accepts_relative_path`
  explicitly asserts an empty plaintext field and the encrypted spawn payload.

An observed existing V2 child rollout had the expected `NEW_TASK` envelope plus
an encrypted content block. Its body was not locally available as plaintext.
Adding an input hook alone therefore does not supply the task needed by the
selector. This report does not claim knowledge of hosted decryption internals.

These are pinned source observations and existing rollout metadata. No
encryption bypass, modified-runtime execution, or new provider experiment was
performed for this request, and the upstream Rust tests were not run.

Suggested acceptance checks: one selector attempt before first response;
zero selector calls or manual summary generation by either agent; native
task-bound outcome; safe duplicate handling; bounded fallback; no unauthorized
export; and unchanged model, reasoning effort, profile, and access limits.

Related existing requests are [#46939](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/46939)
for configurable plaintext delivery and [#28058](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/28058)
for a readable audit trail. The capability requested here is automatic,
task-bound source selection using an authorized public summary while retaining
the encrypted task body. These related requests do not themselves provide
that selector phase.

### Codex App version

Windows AppX package: 26.1007.2314.0.
Versions and timeline below come from our local diagnostic report.

### Subscription
ChatGPT Pro.

### Platform
Windows; exact OS build and architecture were not captured for this report.

### Issue
An existing durable task previously performed local Windows file operations and used native task-messaging tools. After transport/resume failures, both capabilities became unavailable. Incoming messages still reach the task, but native outgoing messaging cannot be attempted because its tool is absent. No outgoing send returned DENIED during this missing-tool episode.

The diagnostic report records environmentIds changing from populated to empty while recorded permissions and the last completed turn remained unchanged. Executor reconnection and a later desktop restart did not restore the task's capabilities. The underlying cause is unknown; chronology alone does not prove causation.

### Observed sequence
This is an observed incident, not a deterministic clean-install reproduction:
1. Continue an existing durable task with working local execution and native messaging.
2. Encounter transport failures and a 30-second thread/resume timeout.
3. Resume the same task and find both capabilities missing.
4. Reconnect the executor, then later restart/reconnect the desktop app.
5. Recheck the same task: environmentIds remains empty and capabilities are not restored.

Timeline, 2026-10-11 UTC:
- 07:38:21.5903325: last successful local write.
- 07:38:48.2145280: last successful local read.
- 07:41:46.163: environmentIds still populated.
- 07:45:53.558: executor reconnect recorded.
- 07:45:58.032: environmentIds empty; recorded permissions and last completed turn unchanged.
- 09:40:33.253: later app restart/reconnect recorded.
- 09:42:17.679: environmentIds still empty.

### Expected behavior
Retain or restore authorized local execution and native messaging after reconnection. Please provide a supported recovery for the SAME task without replacing it or losing its history. If its environment is intentionally deselected, expose the reason and supported recovery steps.

### Related reports
#50800, #50635, and #52854 describe related missing-tool or transport symptoms. This report adds the populated-to-empty environmentIds transition and loss of local execution. A shared root cause is not established; please consolidate with #50800 if appropriate.

Please compare environment-binding revisions, resume responses, and per-turn tool catalogs before and after the transition. Please identify supported read-only diagnostics and recovery steps.
