items.title: [Windows 10 / Codex Work] Remote compaction repeatedly fails across multiple threads (decode error and SSE timeout) since Oct 3

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: context
labels.description: Issues related to context management (including compaction)

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

items.body:
## Summary

Since **2026-10-03**, remote context compaction has repeatedly failed in multiple separate Codex/ChatGPT Work task threads. As of **2026-10-11**, the problem is still blocking the reporter's longer-running technical work. This is not a report of a single corrupted conversation: screenshots show recurring errors in a restored long-running Astra HQ session and in other separate task/project threads. The reporter also observed a recurrence in a newly created thread on **2026-10-07** (date and fresh-thread status from their timeline, not independently timestamped in the screenshots).

The user has a **paid ChatGPT Pro subscription** (reports paying about **USD 117/month**). Shorter, bounded tasks in fresh sessions may still work, but automatic compaction/continuation of substantial tasks remains unreliable, forcing work to be split into smaller sessions and repeatedly reconstructed.

## Environment

- Host: **Windows 10 Pro 22H2**.
- Surface: ChatGPT Codex/Work desktop tasks. Evidence screenshots were captured from the **iOS ChatGPT client**, showing the affected task threads (with a **NIX** workspace label); this does *not* establish that iOS itself causes the failure.
- Agent/model in the affected workflow: **Astra / GPT-6** as selected by the user; errors also appear in several task threads.
- Desktop app builds observed by the reporter during the troubleshooting period: **26.930.79.45.0** and, following an application restart/update, **26.1020.71.24.0**. Per-screenshot build/runtime correlation is **not available**.
- Subscription authentication, thread IDs, backend request IDs, and exact network root cause have **not** been independently extracted. Please advise which safe diagnostic identifiers would help.

## Exact user-visible errors

Most frequent:

```text
Error running remote compact task: stream disconnected before completion: Transport error: network error: error decoding response body
```

Also observed repeatedly in a different thread:

```text
Error running remote compact task: stream disconnected before completion: idle timeout waiting for SSE
```

One task also displayed the transport/decode error without the `Error running remote compact task:` prefix.

## Timeline (user-reported dates; screenshots do not contain full calendar timestamps)

- **Oct 3:** First noticed the persistent remote-compaction failures.
- **Oct 3–6:** Repeated failures in the main long-running Astra HQ / recovery conversation. One screenshot contains three consecutive instances of the same decoding failure.
- **Oct 7:** The reporter says the problem also recurred in a new thread; this is why treating the initial conversation as the sole defective object is not sufficient.
- **Through Oct 11:** Failures persist across multiple conversations, including independent project sessions. Captures include visible context-compaction UI followed by the transport/decode error, and a separate conversation with consecutive SSE idle-timeout errors.

## Reproduction pattern

1. Continue a nontrivial or long-running Codex/Work task in an existing thread.
2. When remote context compaction is invoked, the compact operation does not complete successfully.
3. Instead of reducing context and allowing normal continuation, one of the errors above is displayed.
4. Retrying continuation may produce the same error again. Starting smaller tasks in new sessions is only a partial workaround; it does not preserve the working context of a larger project.

The reporter has **not** established that these failures share a single underlying cause, occur at a fixed context percentage, or are exclusively attributable to the desktop client, network, or VPN.

## Expected vs actual

**Expected:** Automatic/remote context compaction succeeds, or a safe recovery path preserves the session and reports an actionable error.

**Actual:** Compaction fails with transport/decode errors or an SSE idle timeout, preventing reliable continuation of long technical project sessions. A week's worth of attempts has not produced a usable recovery route for the affected workflow.

## Evidence

The reporter supplied **nine screenshots** from affected threads. They show:
- several identical remote-compaction decode failures in a single recovery thread;
- repetition after the UI explicitly shows context compaction;
- a separate project thread exhibiting the same decode failure;
- consecutive `idle timeout waiting for SSE` errors in another thread.

The captures were reviewed in preparing this report. **The GitHub API integration used to open this issue does not support binary screenshot attachments**, so the image files are **not attached to this issue yet**. They can be added through the GitHub web UI; please do not interpret their absence here as an absence of captures. Personal project details should be redacted before public upload.

## Requests to maintainers

1. Is this a known failure mode of **remote compaction / transport streaming** on the current Codex/Work stack? Can maintainers correlate both error families?
2. What **safe, supported workaround** lets a paying user resume existing long-running threads **without deleting or resetting their data**?
3. Which diagnostic identifiers/logs can be collected and shared **privately** for backend correlation, without exposing tokens, conversation contents, or project files?
4. Can you confirm whether a fix is available or being tracked? A generic status page reporting operational service does not resolve this user's repeated compaction failures.

### Related issues

- #45216 — Windows/remote SSH compaction: decode and SSE idle-timeout failures.
- #45472 — Windows Work/Codex remote compaction SSE timeout.
- #50843 — Windows consecutive remote-compaction decode failures.
- #38969 — repeated remote-compaction response decode errors.

This issue is a **distinct user-impact report across multiple sessions**, not a claim that the root cause is already known.

Piping `codex plugin list` into a consumer such as `head` can close stdout before the full catalog is written, causing a panic.

Add unit tests for write and flush failures in both output formats, plus CLI tests that close stdout early and verify a successful exit without a panic.

items.title: Disabled usage-reset setting does not revoke an existing guard using standalone app-server

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: rate-limits
labels.description: Issues related to rate limits, quotas, and token usage reporting

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

Installed desktop app: **26.1007.21159 (build 20052)**. The affected account operation was performed by a separate **codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2** process through `codex app-server --listen stdio://`, not by clicking the desktop reset button. Versions were read during the subsequent investigation; the guard did not record a binary version at redemption time.

### What subscription do you have?

Pro.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS, Apple Silicon. `uname -mprs`: `Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm`.

### What issue are you seeing?

A previously established, Codex-generated subscription guard automatically consumed my last banked usage reset after I had turned **“Allow Codex usage resets” OFF** in the desktop settings. Disabling the setting did not revoke the guard's ability to redeem a reset through the standalone app-server account API.

The guard had historical permission to reset at 1% remaining. I later disabled the system setting because I no longer wanted automatic reset consumption. There was no new confirmation or manual reset action when the credit was consumed.

Local investigation found the setting is explicitly persisted as:

```toml
agent-usage-reset-enabled = false
```

The guard does not consult that setting. It initializes a separate CLI app-server, reads the account's limits, and calls `account/rateLimitResetCredit/consume` when remaining usage is <=1%. The account operation succeeded despite the desktop opt-out.

**Scope of this report:** this was custom, agent-generated automation using a native account API, not evidence that an unmodified desktop UI spontaneously resets accounts. The guard's failure to check the opt-out is a local implementation defect. I am reporting the additional product boundary/consent gap: the user-facing switch did not stop a pre-existing agent-created reset path, and successful redemption did not require a fresh user confirmation. Please clarify whether this setting is only a desktop-agent tool toggle or is intended to govern automated reset redemption across native clients.

### Observed incident and evidence

- **2026-10-11 02:09:41 UTC / 03:09:41 Europe/London:** an actual account-bound guard receipt reports one consume request and outcome `reset`.
- Remaining weekly allowance: **1% -> 100%**.
- Available banked resets: **1 -> 0**.
- Desktop usage-reset history shows the same date and **03:09 GMT+1**.
- The user confirms the switch was off before the incident; post-incident configuration and screenshot confirm it is off. The guard did not save a configuration snapshot at the instant of redemption, so I am not claiming an independently captured before-event setting snapshot.

Redacted receipt excerpt:

```json
{
  "recorded_at": "2026-10-11T02:09:41.041283+00:00",
  "status": "reset",
  "outcome": "reset",
  "threshold_remaining_percent": 1,
  "consume_request_attempts": 1,
  "account_binding_verified": true,
  "snapshot_before": {
    "remaining_percent": 1,
    "available_reset_count": 1
  },
  "snapshot_after": {
    "remaining_percent": 100,
    "available_reset_count": 0
  }
}
```

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The following describes the observed guard's call sequence; **I have not executed another consuming request to reproduce it**, because that would spend another reset. All IDs below are placeholders.

1. Previously allow an agent to establish a guard for a long-running job that resets usage when it reaches 1% remaining.
2. Turn “Allow Codex usage resets” off in desktop settings; the persisted setting is `false`.
3. The existing guard retains its historical configuration/authorization and later initializes an independent CLI app-server for the same logged-in account:

```json
{"id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"clientInfo":{"name":"subscription-guard","version":"1.0"},"capabilities":{"experimentalApi":true}}}
{"method":"initialized","params":{}}
{"id":2,"method":"account/rateLimits/read","params":{"excludeResetCreditDetails":false}}
{"id":3,"method":"account/rateLimitResetCredit/consume","params":{"creditId":"<available-credit-id>","idempotencyKey":"<fresh-uuid>"}}
```

4. At 1% remaining, the native account API accepts the consuming request and the banked credit is spent, without a new action-time confirmation.

### What is the expected behavior?

- Turning automated usage resets off should revoke previously established agent/guard reset permission, including already-running jobs.
- A guard should check current consent immediately before every consuming action; historical conversation permission should not silently survive a later opt-out.
- Native clients should have an explicit, enforceable consent/revocation mechanism for automated reset redemption, while retaining intentional user-initiated manual resets.
- If the desktop toggle intentionally covers only one tool surface, document that limitation clearly and provide a way to revoke existing automated/native reset paths. The present UI gives no warning that such paths can continue consuming credits.
- Please provide a private support route to investigate replacement of the erroneously consumed banked credit.

### Additional information

Related consent reports: #43118 and #41827. This report specifically concerns **revocation after disabling the setting and a pre-existing standalone app-server guard**, rather than initial ambiguous intent or a manual reset click.

The reset path uses the logged-in native account service. No model-provider API was used to redeem the credit. A custom local provider wrapper also exists in this environment; a clean-stock second consuming reproduction has not been attempted. Original logs and the agent-generated guard source are retained privately. Account IDs, reset-credit IDs, credentials, private paths, and unpublished research data are omitted from this issue and can be supplied privately if needed.

items.title: [Windows/WSL] codex_app discovery races renderer readiness; bounded tools/list retry recovers without replaying actions

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Windows package version `26.1007.2314.0` (package metadata, not the About dialog).
App-owned WSL backend observed during the startup investigation: `0.162.0-alpha.17.2`.
A separate managed-daemon session uses `0.162.1`; it is not the same backend.

### What subscription do you have?

Not included; this report concerns locally measured startup/IPC behavior rather than a model-quality comparison.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64 desktop App with a WSL2 agent. Current reporting shell: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, Linux 6.18.40.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64. Exact Windows OS build was not collected for this report.

### What issue are you seeing?

During ordinary desktop startup, the native app-tools pipe can accept requests before its renderer is ready to supply dynamic tools. An early read-only `tools/list` request fails with RPC `-32000`; the corresponding App log reports:

```text
The Codex app renderer is unavailable
```

The transport can expose the failure as `Codex app tool request failed`. Historical natural MCP startup also produced a `codex_app` tools/list timeout after 10 seconds. The direct probe below is separately identified and must not be counted as a natural MCP failure.

Read-only inspection of the installed main-process bundle found a 10,000 ms renderer-response wait, after which the request resolves without a renderer result and the caller reports it unavailable. This establishes a readiness/response-delay boundary, not the exact blocking renderer task or the cause of every reported chat hang. Increasing only an outer MCP startup timeout does not suppress an internal error response.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed diagnostic sequence on this installation; not claimed to be a deterministic clean-install reproducer:

1. Close the installed App and reactivate its registered Windows package normally, keeping WSL and an independent managed daemon running.
2. Observe the native app-tools pipe becoming available.
3. Issue a read-only tools/list request early during startup, then repeat after the renderer has had time to initialize. No tool actions or user messages are needed.
4. Correlate the request result with the App's renderer-unavailable log.

Measured sequence on 2026-10-11 UTC, relative to ordinary package activation:

| Event | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| Pipe starts listening | +17.333 s |
| First tools/list starts | +19.418 s |
| First request fails | 11.052 s request duration; RPC -32000 and renderer-unavailable log |
| Next request | succeeds after 12.936 s; 56 tools |
| Later catalogue | 57 tools |
| Last four warm requests | 32, 44, 25, 33 ms |

The bounded observer made 16 requests: one failure and 15 successes. Polling adds startup work. The 12.936 s successful response also indicates the nominal 10 s wait is not an exact wall-clock limit under startup load; event-loop/IPC delay needs profiling.

### What is the expected behavior?

Desktop-owned tool discovery should wait for a usable renderer, or recover from transient readiness failures with a bounded, cancellable mechanism. A listening pipe should not be treated as complete tool readiness. Failures should distinguish renderer readiness from transport errors and identify the pending startup phase.

Recovery must not automatically replay tools/call or any user action whose outcome is unknown.

### Additional information

#### Applied local workaround and results

We added a user `mcp_servers.codex_app` transport override that runs a small Python stdio adapter in front of the original, unmodified bundled Windows Node/server.mjs transport. The App itself was observed launching this adapter.

The adapter:
- forwards initialize, notifications, context/sandbox metadata and tools/call unchanged;
- retries only tools/list failures matching the observed readiness messages, at 1-second intervals within a 75-second discovery budget;
- uses a 90-second outer MCP startup timeout;
- preserves the packaged approval policy and six explicitly prompt-required tool policies; startup checks for policy drift;
- never retries tool actions, and stops discovery retries on cancellation/deadline.

A valid early-start test reproduced the initial failure and recovered on attempt 2: initialize 2.752 s; tools/list 19.786 s total; 57 tools successfully returned to the client. Audit records distinguish this probe from actual App-owned adapter invocations. Five ordinary package activations after the change had no captured natural MCP/discovery expiry lines in their bounded observation windows.

Unit checks cover metadata passthrough, readiness retries, no action replay and permanent-failure deadline termination. Two earlier observer runs were invalid due to an extra diagnostic field in their JSON-RPC requests; they were corrected and are excluded from acceptance.

This is a local workaround, not a supported vendor fix or proof that all integrations now work.

#### Other changes and remaining boundaries

Before isolating this race, we restored WSL shell/file execution, moved bulk plugin/discovery caches to Linux-native storage, and retained the canonical Windows location plus WSL access for the reserved bundled catalogue. Both catalogues register. These custom cache routes were unchanged across the readiness experiment; no isolated evidence proves cache relocation fixes the renderer race.

Ordinary file work now uses WSL tools; project execution stays in configured Docker. A local routing skill documents this compromise. Windows Node REPL is retained for dependent native integrations, but its separate UNC/EPERM and sandboxCwd local-file-URI errors are not fixed. Independent config/read deadline failures are also not explained by the discovery workaround.

Actual retained tool actions, full chat continuation with the final configuration, real boot and future update acceptance remain open. No packaged code was patched, sandbox weakened, profile/history replaced, or WSL shutdown used for the readiness fix.

Related startup reports include #48466 and #49687; shared root cause is unproven. Unlike a permanent splash-screen hang, this report measures eventual renderer recovery and a discovery-only mitigation. Please consolidate if this belongs to an existing issue.

No raw logs, private paths, usernames, thread IDs, credentials, chat content or full configuration are attached.

labels.name: bug

labels.name: session

items.body:
### What happened

An initially working Codex Cloud environment later became unavailable during snapshot restoration. The setup records reported:

```text
snapshot_restore_exhausted
failed to query executor configuration capabilities
```

The last reported runtime observation was `failed/offline` at revision 18, while the desired state was `running`. This is a recorded observation, not a new live runtime check.

A review of my Windows desktop logs independently confirmed an environment draft-save failure on **2026-10-11 at 08:23:27.919 UTC**:

```text
[environmentConfig] Environment configuration request failed
method=PATCH
route=/v1/environment-configs/:configId/draft
status=500
code=-32603
message="Something went wrong. Request ID: <redacted>"
elapsedMs=2427
```

The local environment catalog identifies the affected saved configuration as the ARC setup. Private configuration and request identifiers are omitted here and supplied to support separately. The save error and restoration error may have different causes; I do not have evidence establishing a common cause.

### Observed sequence

1. Prepare and use a Codex Cloud development environment.
2. Later attempt to resume the existing setup/workspace.
3. Observe snapshot-restoration exhaustion and executor capability-query errors; the recorded runtime remains unavailable.
4. Separately, attempt to save the environment draft; the desktop log records the HTTP 500 above.

This describes the observed sequence, not a deterministic minimal reproduction. I cannot establish which configuration change, if any, triggered restoration failure.

### Expected behavior

The existing workspace should restore and become executable with its saved work and configuration intact. Saving a draft should succeed, or return an actionable error explaining what was saved and how to recover safely.

Please investigate the failed restoration stage, whether the saved snapshot remains recoverable, and whether the draft-save request committed any changes despite returning HTTP 500. A recovery path should preserve uncommitted files, installed tools, and environment settings rather than require deleting the original environment.

### Context

- Platform: Windows, Codex desktop app.
- Installed desktop package: `OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.2314.0`; managed backend/image version unknown.
- Earlier public dataset downloads also encountered proxy HTTP 403 at `us.aws.cdn.hf.co`. This is separate network evidence, not proof of a restoration cause.
- A separate environment's records reported `environment_startup_failed` / `vpn_enrollment_failed`. A related independent report already exists at #50827; this issue focuses on snapshot restoration and draft saving.
- #51434 describes related cloud publishing/resumption and executor-capability symptoms. I cannot confirm these are the same defect.

Environment/runtime identifiers and available diagnostic records can be provided privately. No VPN keys, access tokens, private repository details, or raw logs are included in this public report.

### What issue are you seeing?

While running multiple Codex CLI agents simultaneously, I manually interrupted one of the active conversations to conserve my remaining usage quota.

However, another active agent continued sending messages to the interrupted agent through `codex_tui.send_message_to_thread`.

After receiving these inter-agent messages, the interrupted conversation appeared to resume execution without any new user prompt or authorization.

I had to interrupt the conversation twice. Between interruptions, additional agent activity appeared, including source code modifications.

This occurred while my remaining 5-hour usage quota was below 10%, eventually dropping below 5%.

The behavior raises concerns about user control over agent execution, unintended file modifications, and potentially unauthorized consumption of usage quota.

I cannot confirm whether the messages directly restarted the interrupted agent or whether pending tasks continued running, but the observed behavior strongly suggests an issue with interruption handling and inter-agent communication.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Start two or more Codex CLI tasks with inter-agent communication enabled.
2. Allow the agents to coordinate using `codex_tui.send_message_to_thread`.
3. Manually interrupt one of the active tasks using the Codex CLI interface.
4. Keep another agent running.
5. Have the active agent send a message to the interrupted task using `codex_tui.send_message_to_thread`.
6. Observe whether the interrupted conversation receives the message and resumes generating output or performing tool calls without a new user prompt.
7. If execution resumes, interrupt the conversation again.

In my case, the terminal displayed `Conversation interrupted`, followed by additional inter-agent messages and apparent task activity.

I did not manually resume the interrupted conversation.

This reproduction procedure is based on my observations; I have not independently confirmed that the behavior occurs consistently.

### What is the expected behavior?

When a user explicitly interrupts a Codex task, that task should remain stopped until the user manually resumes it.

Incoming inter-agent messages must not automatically reactivate a user-interrupted conversation.

If another agent attempts to contact an interrupted task, Codex should either queue the message without executing the recipient or return an appropriate status indicating that the recipient has been interrupted.

User-initiated interruption should take precedence over autonomous agent coordination.

No additional tool calls, file modifications, or usage quota consumption should occur in an explicitly stopped task without further user authorization.

### Additional information

**Relevant log excerpts**

Usage warnings:

```
⚠ Heads up, you have less than 10% of your 5h limit left.
⚠ Heads up, you have less than 5% of your 5h limit left.
```

Inter-agent communication:

```
Called codex_tui.send_message_to_thread
{"threadId":"01a11cc7-f480-7bd3-b095-2db2665e85b5"}
```

Manual interruption:

```
■ Conversation interrupted - use /feedback if something went wrong
```

File modifications visible between interruption messages:

```
• Edited 2 files (+15 -1)
  └ homecloud_setup/development_image.py
  └ homecloud_setup/persistence.py
```

A second `Conversation interrupted` message was subsequently displayed.

**Relevant task IDs**
- `01a11cc7-f480-7bd3-b095-2db2665e85b5`
- `01a11768-d92b-7d01-bcd1-92af9e36d234`
- `01a12a9f-8651-7d60-b165-bdf9cde1f435`

**Important clarification**

The logs do not conclusively establish that `send_message_to_thread` itself restarted the stopped process. The behavior could also involve queued messages or background/subagent execution.

However, execution activity appeared after explicit user interruption, without any new user prompt.

This issue is particularly concerning when multiple agents share a limited usage quota, because users may be unable to reliably stop unwanted resource consumption.

items.title: [Linux/Zorin OS 18.1] Codex Desktop shows “Organization settings could not be loaded” on personal Plus account; persists across reinstall, recovers after configuration/runtime reset

items.body:
## Environment
- Zorin OS 18.1 (Ubuntu-based Linux), x86_64
- Codex/ChatGPT desktop .deb package: `chatgpt` 26.1007.21434
- Personal ChatGPT Plus subscription (not a managed enterprise workspace)
- Codex works when accessed through a web browser on the same computer/account

## Symptom
On every desktop launch, a blocking dialog says:

> Organization settings could not be loaded. The app is paused until your organization settings can be loaded safely. A network connection, proxy, or firewall may be preventing access.

The `Retry` action did not resolve it; `Sign out` did not function as expected. This recurred after rebooting and uninstalling/reinstalling the same .deb.

## Troubleshooting observations
- UFW firewall was disabled; system network proxy was off.
- `curl -I https://chatgpt.com` established HTTPS successfully and returned HTTP 405 for HEAD (not a TLS failure).
- The desktop Electron process was running; its user-data directory appeared in the process arguments as `~/.config/Codex`.
- Moving aside `~/.config/Codex` alone did not resolve the startup error.
- No `CODEX_CLI_PATH` override was present in the terminal environment.
- Browser Codex worked normally with the personal Plus account, while the desktop app remained blocked.

## Reported recovery / troubleshooting lead
The user reports that the application was eventually recovered through a **terminal-based reset of persistent Codex configuration and runtime/application state**, without changing the network or purchasing/adding an organizational subscription.

During diagnosis, earlier removal of the local state database (`~/.codex/sqlite/codex-dev.db`) and `~/.codex/.codex-global-state.json` was reported **not** to resolve the error on its own. Subsequent troubleshooting included moving existing `~/.codex*` configuration directories out of the application's normal location (into a separate backup) and clearing `~/.cache/codex-runtimes` and `~/.local/state/codex`. The user reported that the desktop issue was resolved in this sequence, but **the independently necessary step was not isolated**, so this is a reported recovery path rather than a verified universal fix.

**Caution:** Resetting these locations can remove local sessions, history/state, cached runtimes, and diagnostics. Users should back up relevant local data first; this report is not advising indiscriminate deletion.

## Possible cause — unverified
During troubleshooting, another assistant suggested a possible `service_tier` / personal-vs-commercial organization-context mismatch that led the app to request enterprise organization policy for a personal Plus account. **This was not demonstrated from a captured config value or backend trace; please treat it as a hypothesis, not a proven root cause.**

The generic network/firewall dialog may be masking an initialization, account-context, or local-state failure. The user-data/configuration reset was substantially more relevant than reinstalling the package.

## Requested developer follow-up
1. Check whether stale Linux desktop Codex state/runtime caches or account/workspace selection can trigger organization-policy loading on personal ChatGPT subscriptions.
2. Surface a specific backend/configuration error instead of a generic network/proxy/firewall message when those systems are healthy.
3. Document a supported, non-destructive reset/recovery path that preserves user projects/history.

### Related symptom reports
- #50974 (Windows desktop organization-settings loop)
- #51586 (organization-settings failure despite reinstall/browser or CLI login)
- #48324 (browser functional, desktop fails to load organization settings)

No usernames, tokens, account identifiers, project paths, or personal screenshots are included in this report.

### What issue are you seeing?

## [BUG] Fullscreen: mouse wheel dead zone below top ~1/3 of viewport — only on 225% HiDPI display (Windows Terminal → SSH)

### Environment
- codex-cli 0.162.1 (installed via curl install script)
- Remote: Ubuntu (Linux 6.8, Azure VM) via OpenSSH from PowerShell
- Local: Windows Terminal on Windows 11
- Config: `tui.fullscreen_transcript = true`, everything else at defaults
  (alternate_screen and mouse_scroll_speed both tested explicitly — see below)
- Displays: laptop built-in screen at 225% Windows display scaling;
  external monitor at 100% (scaling locked)
- Terminal size (`stty size`): laptop 40 rows × 142 cols; external
  (maximized) 51 rows × 209 cols

### Symptom
In fullscreen transcript mode, the mouse wheel scrolls only while the
cursor is in approximately the **top 1/3 of the viewport**; wheel events
below that horizontal line are silently ignored.

Concrete measurement: with a 40-row terminal (`stty size` = 40 142) and a
transcript of numbered lines 1–50, the boundary sits **exactly at row 14**
— i.e. scrollable region height ≈ rows/3 (40/3 ≈ 13.3). The boundary is
proportional: resizing the window repaints correctly, but the boundary
stays at ~1/3 of the new height. It is unrelated to transcript content and
is also present in the Ctrl+T transcript overlay. Keyboard scrolling
(arrows/PgUp/PgDn) works normally in all areas.

### Ruled out by A/B testing
- **Content-independent**: the boundary does not move w
- `fullscreen_transcript = false` → wheel works over the whole window;
  the bug is specific to fullscreen mode's own wheel handling.
- `tui.alternate_screen` = auto/always/never: no effect
- `tui.mouse_scroll_speed` (tested with the key removed entirely): no
  effect; boundary stays at row 14 of 40. The coincidence of "rows/3"
  and a previously tested `mouse_scroll_speed = 3` is r
- Reproduces identically inside tmux (`set -g mouse on`,
  `TERM=tmux-256color`) and over bare SSH → not a TERM/terminal-
  negotiation issue.
- **Drag selection lands at the correct position in the dead zone** →
  mouse coordinates are reported correctly; this is NOT a DPI coordinate-
  scaling bug (225% scaling would also predict a ~44% b
  observed ~33%). Only *wheel* events are filtered.
- **Strictly display-environment-dependent**: on the ex
  monitor the dead zone never appears — **even maximized at 51 rows,
  larger than the laptop's 40 rows**. Terminal dimensions are therefore
  not the trigger; the laptop's HiDPI display context is.
- Claude Code CLI's fullscreen mode scrolls correctly o
  terminal/SSH/display setup → wheel events reach the remote application
  intact; the filtering happens inside Codex.

### Hypothesis for maintainers
Codex (or crossterm) may derive its wheel-scroll hit re
query that returns different values under per-monitor DPI on the laptop
display (e.g. pixel metrics from TIOCGWINSZ/XTWINOPS vs. cell geometry),
producing a scroll region ~1/3 of the actual viewport height. The measured
boundary (rows/3) suggests a 3× factor entering a pixel
somewhere in the scroll-region calculation under the HiDPI display context
(the display is set to 225% scaling, but the effective DPI bucket Windows
applies may differ).

### Related issues
- #36099, #9027 (wheel scroll failures — but no spatial dead-zone pattern
  reported there)
- #48434 (wheel redraw backlog — I also see flicker on fast scrolling,
  mitigated by running inside tmux; likely a separate i

### Expected
Wheel scrolling works regardless of cursor position, as
100%-scaling monitor.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Setup: Windows 11, Windows Terminal, OpenSSH (from PowerShell) into a
remote Ubuntu VM. Local display = laptop built-in screen at 225% Windows
display scaling. Codex config: `tui.fullscreen_transcript = true`
(everything else default).

1. SSH into the remote host with the Windows Terminal window on the
   225%-scaling laptop display.
2. Start `codex` (fullscreen transcript mode).
3. Generate a transcript longer than the screen, e.g. ask:
   "print 1 to 50, each on its own line".
4. Hover the mouse over the **top ~1/3** of the window and scroll the
   wheel → transcript scrolls.
5. Hover anywhere **below that line** and scroll → nothing happens.

Concrete measurement: at 40 terminal rows (`stty size` = 40 142), the
dead zone boundary sits exactly at row 14, i.e. scrollable region
height ≈ rows/3.

Control: move the same window to an external monitor at 100% scaling →
wheel scrolls over the entire viewport, even maximized
(larger than the laptop's 40). Move it back to the laptop display →
dead zone returns. Keyboard scrolling (arrows/PgUp/PgDn) works
everywhere in all cases.


### What is the expected behavior?

Mouse-wheel scrolling should scroll the fullscreen transcript regardless
of where the cursor is positioned in the window — as it does when the
window is on the 100%-scaling external monitor, and as other fullscreen
TUI apps (e.g. Claude Code CLI) do on the same terminal/display setup.

### Additional information

_No response_

items.title: [Cloud Browser] YouTube watch page stalls at 0:00 (readyState=0) on a public video

labels.name: bug

labels.description: Issues related to Codex Web

items.body:
### Summary

A public YouTube video can load normally in the Codex/assistant cloud browser (title, channel, description, duration, controls), but media playback never advances from 0:00. This blocked direct visual/audio verification during a research workflow.

Observed on 2026-10-11.

Public test video:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tlCeLkw8Upc

### Observed behavior

On the normal YouTube watch page:

- the 1:06 player is rendered
- clicking the normal Play control changes the player state, but playback does not advance
- the screen remains black/buffering at 0:00

Recorded DOM/media state after the play interaction:

```text
video.currentTime = 0
video.readyState = 0
video.paused = false
video.error = null
```

The normal UI was also tried with Auto, 720p, and 360p quality without playback progress.

A YouTube iframe embedded in a host page likewise displayed the 66-second player but remained at 0:00.

### Important control / non-root-cause observation

Opening `https://www.youtube.com/embed/<id>` as a top-level page produced YouTube error 153.

Per YouTube's documented IFrame Player API behavior, error 153 indicates that the request does not include the HTTP Referer header or equivalent API-client identity. A top-level embed URL may therefore be an invalid comparison path, so I am **not** treating that 153 response as the root cause of the normal watch-page stall.

The bug report is specifically about the ordinary watch page and a normal hosted iframe failing to obtain/play media.

### Separate browser-surface observation

A native cloud Chromium / Computer Use path could open and inspect the browser surface, but the navigation attempt then encountered a separate CUA/Sky `AT-SPI provider unavailable` error before the target video could be reached. I am not counting that as an additional YouTube-playback reproduction.

### Expected behavior

For a public video that is viewable in a normal supported browser, the watch-page player should receive media, render frames/audio, and advance `currentTime`.

If media playback is unsupported or blocked in this cloud environment, the browser/tooling should return an actionable reason instead of exposing a normal player UI that remains indefinitely at 0:00.

### Impact

This prevents direct verification of:

- scene order / cuts
- timestamps
- spoken lines and voice
- BGM / audio
- visual details that are only present in the video

Static fallback sources (the official site, official X post, title/description, and official still images) remained readable, but they cannot substitute for direct video verification.

### Requested investigation

Could you please check:

1. whether the cloud browser is receiving the YouTube media/manifest requests on the watch page;
2. why `readyState` remains 0 while `paused=false` and `error=null`;
3. whether authentication, proxy/network policy, media codecs/decoding, or the browser automation layer prevents media delivery;
4. whether the supported browser surface can expose a specific media-playback error when this happens.

### Privacy

This report contains only a public video URL and minimal player-state values. It omits account identity, cookies, tokens, authentication headers, signed media URLs, local filesystem paths, and private conversation data.

items.title: [Dots] Network/proxy mismatch between manual cloud terminal and agent execution blocks user handoff

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: auth
labels.description: Issues related to authentication and accounts

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

labels.name: dots
labels.description: Issues involving setting up ChatGPT dots or managing their ongoing work.

items.body:
## Problem

On the same dot cloud computer, the user-operated desktop terminal and the agent's command-execution environment have different network behavior and proxy configuration. Requests from the manual terminal fail, while HTTP probes to the same host and endpoint through agent execution receive responses.

This blocks the user handoff workflow.

## Observed differences

1. The manual terminal has no HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, NO_PROXY or corresponding lowercase environment variables.
2. Agent execution has proxy variables pointing to loopback addresses. The assigned ports change across separate execution contexts.
3. A manually launched CLI fails on an HTTPS request with `connect: connection refused`, exiting with code 3.
4. Agent execution receives HTTP 302 for a HEAD request to the same host and HTTP 400 with a missing-parameter response for an unauthenticated empty POST to the same endpoint.

## Practical impact

In my experience, dots' safety review is overly conservative: many commands and scripts I explicitly ask it to execute still cannot be run directly by dots, so I am asked to perform them manually.

However, the cloud terminal used for that handoff lacks the proxy configuration available in agent execution, and its network requests fail. This leaves both the automatic-execution route and the manual-handoff route unable to complete the task.

Copying a proxy port from an earlier execution is not a usable stable configuration when those ports change between execution contexts.

## Earlier environment changes and file loss

This dot's cloud environment has previously changed several times, with substantial file loss and regressions to older file contents. The current networking/proxy configuration problem may be related to files lost after the previous environment reset. Please also investigate the environment-restoration process.

My earlier file-loss and rollback observations were submitted here:
https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49682#issuecomment-5946815706

## Expected behavior

Please provide a working, supported network configuration for the manual cloud terminal so users can complete steps handed over to them.

If the two execution entry points have different network permissions or configuration requirements, make those differences clear at handoff and provide an actionable path to complete the operation.

## Concrete reproduction example and evidence

The following CLI authorization attempt is one example of the execution-context mismatch described above.

- ChatGPT dots, hosted cloud computer
- User accessing the conversation through iOS
- CLI used in this example: official Feishu `lark-cli 1.0.97`
- Observed October 11, 2026; all times below are UTC
- The affected terminal is on the cloud computer, not my personal computer

### Manual cloud terminal

Running a script that invokes the official CLI's personal authorization flow repeatedly fails at the device-authorization request, before an authorization link is obtained:

```text
device authorization failed: Post "https://accounts.feishu.cn/oauth/v1/device_authorization": dial tcp 98.96.213.145:443: connect: connection refused
```

The CLI exits with code 3.

A diagnostic run at **10:23:18–10:23:19 UTC** recorded:

- Local preflight completed and the CLI process started
- HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, NO_PROXY and their lowercase variants were all absent
- LARK_CLI_NO_PROXY, LARKSUITE_CLI_PROXY_ENABLE, LARKSUITE_CLI_PROXY_ADDRESS and LARKSUITE_CLI_PROXY_CA_PATH were absent
- Failure stage: device authorization
- Error category: connection_refused
- Exit code: 3

### Agent command-execution tool

The ordinary agent execution context had standard proxy environment variables set, pointing to loopback proxies. The assigned ports changed across separate execution contexts.

At **10:27:41–10:27:45 UTC**, this public, unauthenticated request returned HTTP 302 and curl exit code 0:

```sh
curl -q -I --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 15 https://accounts.feishu.cn/
```

At **10:28:27–10:28:32 UTC**, an empty POST to the actual device-authorization endpoint returned HTTP 400 and curl exit code 0:

```sh
curl -q -sS --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 20 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data '' \
  https://accounts.feishu.cn/oauth/v1/device_authorization
```

Response:

```json
{"error":"invalid_request","error_description":"The request is missing a required parameter: client_id.","code":20063}
```

The empty POST contains no application credentials or authorization tokens.

## Reproduction sequence

1. Use an installed official lark-cli on the dot cloud computer.
2. Have the user run the personal OAuth login script in the cloud desktop terminal.
3. Observe the device-authorization connection-refused error and exit code 3.
4. Check whether proxy variables are present in that terminal, without printing any credential values.
5. Run the public HEAD and empty POST above through the dot's agent command-execution tool and compare the results.


## Related reports

- #52239: cloud-desktop networking
- #50381: GUI-versus-agent execution contexts

No credentials, tokens, authorization codes, private tenant URLs or private files are included in this report.

## Environment
- Codex CLI 0.154 on Linux/WSL
- Repository on a mounted Windows volume (DrvFs)

## Steps to reproduce
1. Use a Codex client-side pull-on-touch adapter whose `pull_preflight` runs `git status --porcelain` for a repository.
2. On a mounted Windows volume, that status call takes ~6.7 seconds.

## Actual result
The adapter hard-codes a 5-second subprocess timeout. A clean repository is treated as a broken protection hook, and unrelated read-only tool calls are blocked before execution.

## Expected result
The safety preflight completes on supported mounted-volume installations while preserving the full dirty-worktree check.

## Locally verified fix
Use a named 15-second Git preflight timeout for both status and git-path resolution. Keep untracked-file detection enabled. With this change the adapter suite passes all 13 tests, and the previously blocked live status command completes.

---
Forwarded from a downstream report (originally filed against a template repository that does not contain this adapter code). Reporter verified the fix locally; filing here so the timeout can be addressed where the adapter actually ships.

items.body:
## Summary

All 14 local projects disappeared from the Windows desktop app's Projects sidebar on October 11, 2026. Restarting the app did not restore them. Existing chats and source folders remained available.

This report is filed at the affected user's explicit request. It adds observations from build 13901 and a successful recovery to the similar open report #42739. Please consolidate with that report if appropriate.

## Environment

- Windows desktop app, installed package observed during diagnosis: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1007.2314.0_x64`.
- Desktop client version observed in logs: `26.1007.21434`.
- Build: `13901`.
- Build commit: `615adb2c04224ce3b678e72cd9e6927ce72331f5`.
- Observed date: October 11, 2026.
- Exact trigger and clean-profile reproduction steps are unknown; an update-triggered regression is not established.

## Actual behavior and local evidence

1. The Projects section was empty; the built-in `list_projects` tool returned `{"schemaVersion":2,"projects":[]}`.
2. The built-in `list_threads` still returned existing local chats, with null project IDs in the inspected entries.
3. A local snapshot of `state_5.sqlite` contained 14 rows in `projects`, with corresponding roots in `project_roots`. All project membership counts were zero when joining `threads.project_id` against those projects in that snapshot.
4. `.codex-global-state.json` contained `local-projects: {}` and an empty `sidebar-project-thread-orders`. The local migration checkpoint had `projectsMigrated: true`, `threadAssignmentsMigrated: false`.
5. Desktop startup logged successful project migration with the same count, despite the empty sidebar:

```text
2026-10-11T10:17:30.762Z info [host-app-server-projects] Local app-server project migration completed projectCount=14
```

6. Reconstructing the global-state project cache while Desktop remained open was immediately overwritten: a subsequent read again found zero cached projects.
7. Restarting Desktop alone did not fix the missing projects.

## Recovery performed

After preserving settings and a database snapshot, a local helper was prepared to restore the global-state project cache while Desktop was fully closed. It reconstructed project names, IDs, roots, ordering and available appearance metadata from the existing SQLite records; merged thread assignments for exact normalized working-directory matches while excluding explicitly projectless chats; and reset the thread-assignment migration checkpoints. It did not recreate project source folders or directly modify the live SQLite database.

The user ran the helper with Desktop closed, reopened the app, and confirmed that the projects returned. Because multiple cache/membership fields were restored together, this does not isolate which individual field is necessary for recovery. Durability across future updates or repeated restarts has not been established.

## Expected behavior / investigation request

Existing local projects and their organization should remain visible across launches. If the desktop cache is empty while app-server still has project records, the app should reconcile the cache or expose an actionable recovery state.

Please investigate the project registry/cache reconciliation and incomplete thread-assignment migration. The observed cache/database mismatch is established; the exact root cause remains a hypothesis.

No private project names, user paths, account or thread identifiers, credentials, raw database files, or full session transcripts are attached.

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex CLI 0.162.1 fails to execute any tools, every tool call fails with:

```text
ERROR codex_core::tools::router: error=code-mode host closed its stdout
```

This problem appeared after updating Codex. Version 0.160.0 works correctly on the same machine, using the same model (`gpt-6.1-sol`), configuration, and working directory.

The machine has a restricted virtual address space:

```text
$ ulimit -Sv
840000000
$ ulimit -Hv
840000000
```

Tracing the failing process with `strace` reveals:

```text
mmap(0x51700000000, 1481763713024, PROT_NONE,
     MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS|MAP_NORESERVE, -1, 0)
     = -1 ENOMEM (Cannot allocate memory)

--- SIGSEGV {si_signo=SIGSEGV, si_code=SEGV_MAPERR,
             si_addr=0xb7c9001b5262} ---

+++ killed by SIGSEGV (core dumped) +++
```

The code-mode host attempts to reserve approximately 1.35 TiB of virtual address space, exceeding the process's ~801 GiB `RLIMIT_AS`, and subsequently crashes with SIGSEGV.

This closely resembles the behavior reported in #43820, but in my case this appears to be a regression introduced between versions 0.160.0 and 0.162.1, as version 0.160.0 continues to work correctly.

Restarting the managed app-server daemon, terminating all Codex-related processes, and starting fresh sessions did not resolve the issue.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On a Linux system with a restricted virtual address space (in my case, `RLIMIT_AS = 840000000 KiB`), install Codex CLI 0.162.1 with Code Mode enabled.

2. Run a simple tool-execution prompt:

   ```bash
   codex exec --skip-git-repo-check "Run the shell command pwd and report its output"
   ```

3. Observe that the command is never executed. Instead, Codex reports:

   ```text
   ERROR codex_core::tools::router: error=code-mode host closed its stdout
   ```

   The error occurs twice before Codex gives up.

4. To inspect the underlying crash, run:

   ```bash
   strace -f -e trace=mmap,mmap2 -o /tmp/codex-mmap.log \
     codex exec --skip-git-repo-check "Run the shell command pwd"
   ```

   Then examine:

   ```bash
   grep -E 'ENOMEM|SIGSEGV|killed by' /tmp/codex-mmap.log
   ```

   The trace reveals a failed ~1.35 TiB virtual memory reservation (`ENOMEM`), followed by `SIGSEGV`.

5. For comparison, execute the same prompt using Codex CLI 0.160.0 under the same environment and memory limits. Tool execution succeeds normally.

### What is the expected behavior?

Tool execution succeeds normally.

### Additional information

_No response_

labels.name: enhancement

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Desktop App

### What feature would you like to see?

## Summary

I'd like to request two quality-of-life improvements for the Codex Desktop app:

1. **Automatically group Git branches and worktrees under their parent repository.**
2. **Support a `/clear` command that resets conversation context without changing the current project, worktree, or branch.**

These features would significantly improve the experience for developers running multiple concurrent AI coding sessions.

## Current Problem

I actively use both Claude Code and Codex for large-scale ERP and developer-tool projects, with multiple Git worktrees and long-running development sessions.

My workflow involves more than 10 concurrent development branches across two main repositories.

### 1. Worktree Organization

Claude Code automatically groups sessions belonging to the same Git repository under a single project category.

For example:

**NexusForge**
- Materials
- Logistics
- Accounting
- AI
- Production

**SchemaForge**
- TOW
- EXT
- ERD
- VRF
- API
- QA

This makes it easy to navigate between development sessions.

In Codex Desktop, however, I currently have to add each worktree as a separate project.

As a result, worktrees belonging to the same repository appear as separate top-level projects, making the sidebar increasingly cluttered and difficult to navigate.

Manually rearranging projects helps somewhat, but it does not solve the underlying organizational problem.

### 2. Missing /clear Functionality

Claude Code supports `/clear`, which resets the conversation context while preserving the current working environment.

This is extremely useful for long-running AI development sessions.

In Codex Desktop, starting a fresh conversation while retaining the exact worktree setup is unnecessarily cumbersome in my current workflow.

I often have to create or select a new session and reconfigure its worktree or branch association.

When managing many parallel development sessions, this becomes a significant productivity issue.

## Expected Behavior

### Feature A: Automatic Repository Grouping

- Automatically identify the parent Git repository of each worktree.
- Group all associated worktrees and branches under one collapsible repository category.
- Preserve independent sessions for each worktree.
- Automatically update the grouping when new worktrees are added.
- Avoid requiring users to manually register every worktree as a separate top-level project.

### Feature B: Reset Conversation Context

Provide a `/clear` command or equivalent UI action that:

- Clears the current conversation context.
- Starts a fresh conversation within the same project and worktree.
- Preserves the current working directory and Git branch.
- Does not modify any source files or Git state.
- Does not require users to recreate their development environment.

## Why This Matters

My development workflow uses both Claude Code and Codex concurrently.

Multiple independent AI agents handle development, QA, verification, and code review. Sessions can run for extended periods, and context resets are sometimes necessary to maintain reasoning quality.

Codex has become an essential part of my development workflow because of its strong performance in business logic, UI/UX, and user-oriented application development.

However, project organization and session lifecycle management remain noticeably less convenient than in Claude Code.

For developers managing many repositories, worktrees, and long-running agents, these are not merely cosmetic improvements. They directly affect productivity and operational efficiency.

## Screenshots

**Screenshot 1 — Claude Code**

Shows automatic grouping of multiple development sessions under their respective repositories.

[Attach Claude Code screenshot here]

**Screenshot 2 — Codex Desktop**

Shows the current project/worktree organization and the resulting sidebar clutter.

[Attach Codex Desktop screenshot here]

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Application: Codex Desktop
- Workflow: Multiple repositories, Git worktrees, concurrent long-running AI development sessions

## Final Thoughts

Codex's coding capabilities are excellent, and I now use it alongside Claude Code as a core development tool.

These two improvements would make Codex Desktop significantly more practical for developers managing complex, multi-agent workflows.

Thank you for considering this request.

### Additional information

_No response_

## Request
Allow users to state an outcome once and have ChatGPT **plan and coordinate subtasks across Chat, Work, and Codex** without manual mode switching or repeated context.

This builds on #46836 (unifying the experience). The distinct request here is **execution orchestration**, not just a unified UI or shared workspace.

## Example
> Audit this repository, fix security issues, run tests, and produce a PDF report.

ChatGPT would scope the request → delegate repository changes and tests to Codex → use Work to prepare the report → return one consolidated result.

## Suggested behavior
- Route each subtask based on capabilities and available tools, with a visible execution plan.
- Carry context, decisions, and artifacts across handoffs.
- Explain local/cloud execution and obtain explicit approval for sensitive or consequential actions.
- Start with **recommended routing and one-click handoff** as an MVP; offer optional user-authorized orchestration later.

Related: #49087 addresses usage-aware mode recommendations; this proposal focuses on coordinating execution across modes.

items.body:
### Summary

`/recap` fails when an MCP server is defined only through `-c` overrides. Observed twice with `codex-cli 0.162.1` on macOS 15.5 arm64. The isolated configuration-only reproduction below does not require a running MCP server or a model request.

Sanitized recap log excerpt (server name replaced with `example`):

```text
failed to start thread recap request
thread/start failed: failed to load configuration: invalid transport
in `mcp_servers.example`
(code -32600)
```

### Minimal reproduction

This mirrors the original CLI server definition followed by the temporary recap thread's override:

```sh
env CODEX_HOME="$(mktemp -d)" codex \
  -c 'mcp_servers.example={command="/usr/bin/true"}' \
  -c 'mcp_servers={example={enabled=false}}' \
  features list
```

Configuration loading exits 1 with `invalid transport in mcp_servers.example`, before any MCP process or inference is needed.

We also verified:

- The same failure with an unrelated CLI-defined HTTP server (`url="https://example.invalid/mcp"`).
- The same disable override loads successfully when the complete server definition is in the temporary `config.toml` instead of a CLI override.

### Cause and expected behavior

Code links are pinned to the tested `rust-v0.162.1` commit:

- [`temporary_structured_request.rs:129–137`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d/codex-rs/tui/src/temporary_structured_request.rs#L129-L137) supplies a whole `mcp_servers` override containing only `{ enabled: false }` for each server.
- [`config_manager.rs:446–455`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d/codex-rs/app-server/src/config_manager.rs#L446-L455) appends request overrides to CLI overrides; [`overrides.rs:64`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d/codex-rs/config/src/overrides.rs#L64) replaces that path's value. This discards CLI-only transport definitions.
- [`mcp_types.rs:543`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d/codex-rs/config/src/mcp_types.rs#L543) rejects the remaining entry because it has neither `command` nor `url`, even though it is disabled.

Expected: temporary recap threads disable MCP servers while retaining valid transport definitions. A regression test should cover servers supplied only through `-c`, alongside the config-file case. The same replacement is still present on [main at `8c0f701`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8c0f7011674145da7e10627769fb221c74fbf7a0/codex-rs/tui/src/temporary_structured_request.rs#L129-L137).

items.title: Support xdg-open host bridges for opening links in headless Linux containers

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: TUI
labels.description: Issues related to the terminal user interface: text input, menus and dialogs, and terminal display

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

Codex reports that no valid browsers are detected in a Linux development container even though an executable `xdg-open` is available on PATH and provides URL opening through a host bridge.

The reported error is:

```text
Failed to open browser for <URL>: No valid browsers detected. You can specify one in BROWSER environment variable
```

An installed browser binary inside the container should not be necessary when the standard `xdg-open` entry point is available. In this environment, `xdg-open` is a symlink to `host-open`, which forwards URL/file-opening requests to the host operating system. This is intentional, not a broken desktop installation.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Run Codex CLI in a Linux container with no local graphical browser, with `BROWSER` unset.
2. Make an executable `xdg-open` available on PATH that forwards opening requests to the host. Our environment already supplies this.
3. Attempt to open a URL from Codex's interface. The user observed the error above for a GitLab pipeline link shown by Codex.

Environment checks made after the report:

```text
$ codex --version
codex-cli 0.162.1

$ command -v xdg-open
/riscos-resources/Install/Tools/Linux/xdg-open

$ file /riscos-resources/Install/Tools/Linux/xdg-open
symbolic link to /riscos-resources/Install/Tools/Linux/host-open
```

`host-open` is an executable shell script implementing a host-bridge OPEN request. `BROWSER`, `DISPLAY` and `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` are unset. The container is Linux x86_64 (LinuxKit).

### What is the expected behavior?

Recognise an executable `xdg-open` on PATH as a valid URL-opening mechanism and attempt to use it, even without a local browser binary or local graphical session. Host bridges and remote/container environments can provide a functioning opener without DISPLAY or WAYLAND_DISPLAY.

If the opener itself fails, report its actual failure rather than declaring that no browser is available without trying it. Setting `BROWSER=host-open` should be an optional override, not a requirement when `xdg-open` already exists.

### Additional information

Related: #52766 reports the same error when clicking URLs over SSH. This report focuses specifically on detecting and using an available `xdg-open` host bridge, rather than on preserving the terminal's native click handling.

The exact internal call site and browser-detection condition have not been identified. The original URL-opening error was reported by the user; the PATH, symlink, environment and CLI-version checks above were verified afterward. No claim is made that the GitLab CLI emitted the error.

### Summary

On 2026-10-11, an owner-authorized, read-only delegated review-preparation task in a native Windows Codex environment failed with a possible cybersecurity-risk notice.

This is a suspected false positive or insufficiently actionable safety interruption, not a confirmed classifier defect. We are requesting supported investigation and recovery, not disabled safeguards, alternate execution to evade a refusal, or permission expansion.

### Requested work

The delegated agent was asked to prepare for an independent review of a future exact-commit development candidate in a user-owned local software repository. The request explicitly prohibited execution, tests, source writes and new agents. At that point, no frozen candidate existed.

The surrounding project uses isolated development worktrees, deterministic local fixtures, preserved source identities and mandatory independent reviews. No external target probing, exploit development, real credential access, production access, live provider/model activation or deployment was requested by the affected review-preparation task.

### Actual notice

```text
This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk. If this seems wrong, try rephrasing your request. If you're doing authorized security work that requires more cyber permissive safeguards, apply for Daybreak access via https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/status-and-access before retrying.
```

The delegated agent errored and returned no independent review verdict. The affected preparation was stopped. We have not rephrased or reassigned that blocked request, disabled safeguards, or treated completed development tests as independent acceptance.

Separately permitted implementation subsequently produced a preserved candidate and passing offline development tests; these do not clear the blocked independent-review requirement.

### Environment and diagnostic limitations

- Native Windows x64; current host reports Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0.
- Currently installed bundled executable reports `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2`.
- These version/OS values were checked while preparing this report; the exact affected delegated-agent backend/model and desktop-app build were not independently captured.
- Incident date: 2026-10-11. Exact incident timestamp and request ID are not available in the preserved error record.
- No in-product feedback upload has been submitted from this tool environment. This GitHub issue does not claim to be such an upload or confer clearance.
- No source code, full prompt, session transcript, local paths, credentials, logs or private repository identifiers are attached.

### Expected behavior / questions

1. Can this narrowly scoped read-only software-review preparation be investigated as a possible false positive?
2. If the restriction is intentional, is Daybreak/Trusted Access required for this specific kind of local task, and on which supported surface?
3. What evidence or diagnostic identifier should the account owner provide through the official feedback channel?
4. What explicit supported confirmation would allow the preserved review workflow to resume without weakening safeguards?

Similar symptoms, not an established common cause: #52866 and #50576.

items.body:
### Variant
Codex in the macOS desktop conversation interface, including multiple tasks and forwarded/delegated updates.

### Problem
A user interacting with several Codex tasks could not reliably tell which agent was speaking, who owned the work, or whether a forwarded update was an instruction. During one voice-related workflow, three Codex tasks were involved, while a later snapshot showed two active and one idle. The user repeatedly asked how many agents they were talking to and who was giving orders.

Differences in voice, tone, or response wording are insufficient identity signals. A task count is also ambiguous unless it distinguishes currently active tasks, historically involved tasks, and agents the user actually addressed.

### Requested behavior
1. Show a persistent speaker identity on each assistant reply: agent/task name, stable identity, and execution host/environment.
2. Give forwarded updates an explicit source identity and destination/owner. Distinguish direct user instructions, forwarded requests, and another agent's suggestions.
3. Show one accountable owner per deliverable and the status of collaborating tasks, with the observation time.
4. Make switches and handoffs visible and accessible in text; optionally speak a brief identity announcement in voice sessions. Do not require the user to recognize voices.
5. Keep accepted/completed/verified statuses distinct so a coordination message does not imply that execution or delivery succeeded.

### Example acceptance case
With three tasks involved and two currently active, the user can identify the speaker and current owner from the reply, see the sending task on any forwarded update, and get a count explicitly labeled as active versus involved. Handoff identity remains visible even when every task uses the same voice.

### Local mitigation and limits
The user authorized adding identification and ownership instructions to shared Codex AGENTS.md. That can guide agent responses but does not implement persistent application badges or guarantee that already running or remote sessions have loaded the updated guidance.

### Environment and evidence
Installed macOS desktop bundle version 26.1007.30912, build 20156; macOS 27.0.1 arm64. This request comes from the user's explicit coordination complaint and repeated identity questions in the same workflow. No private transcript, task IDs, local paths, screenshot, or raw logs are included.

Related #48339 addresses cross-account project collaboration; this request focuses on speaker attribution and ownership clarity within one user's multi-task experience.

items.title: Comment reply written by Codex produces a .docx that Word refuses to open (wrong commentsExtended content type) and a reply Word does not show

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: model-behavior
labels.description: Issues related to behaviors exhibited by the model

labels.name: exec
labels.description: Issues related to the `codex exec` subcommand

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?
0.160.0 (npm `@openai/codex`, native `linux-arm64` build, in a container)

### What subscription do you have?
ChatGPT Plus

### Which model were you using?
`gpt-6.1-sol` (the 0.160.0 default with a ChatGPT login on 2026-10-02, pinned with `-m`)

### What platform is your computer?
Linux arm64 container (Docker on macOS); `codex exec`, non-interactive

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?
Not applicable (`codex exec --json`)

### Codex doctor report
Not captured for these runs.

### What issue are you seeing?

Asked to reply to an existing comment in a `.docx`, Codex wrote its own Python
that edits the package directly and declared the new `word/commentsExtended.xml`
part as

```xml
<Override PartName="/word/commentsExtended.xml"
          ContentType="application/vnd.ms-word.commentsExtended+xml"/>
```

with the relationship type `http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/2011/relationships/commentsExtended`.
Word writes `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.commentsExtended+xml`
for that relationship. Word for Mac 16.113.4 refuses the file: "Word found
unreadable content in …"; answering No gives "Word experienced an error trying
to open the file". LibreOffice opens it. This happened in 5 of 5 runs of the
same task.

Separately, the reply itself (linked to its parent through `w15:paraIdParent`)
has no `commentRangeStart`/`commentRangeEnd`/`commentReference` in
`word/document.xml`, so even once the file opens, Word does not show the reply.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Source document: https://github.com/Dmitry-Kov/ooxml-integrity/blob/main/corpus/base.docx
2. `codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check -C /work -m gpt-6.1-sol "<prompt>"` with
   the document at `/work/input.docx` and the output expected at `/work/output.docx`. Prompt:

   > As 'Benchmark Editor', reply to the comment 'Defined term must match the
   > definitions schedule.' with 'Checked against the definitions schedule.' Then
   > add a new comment on '30 days' in the sentence 'Invoices are payable within
   > 30 days.' with the text 'Confirm the payment term with finance.' Do not
   > change anything else.

3. Open the output in Word.

The five outputs, the agent logs and single-change variants are public:
- outputs: `evidence/review-history-benchmark/captures/codex-{1..5}/K5-S1-comment.docx`
- variants of codex-2's output: only the content type corrected (Word opens it,
  the reply is still not shown), and the content type corrected plus the reply
  anchored at its parent's range (Word opens it and shows the reply in the
  thread): `evidence/review-history-benchmark/word-check-content-type/`
  (https://github.com/Dmitry-Kov/ooxml-integrity/tree/main/evidence/review-history-benchmark/word-check-content-type)

### What is the expected behavior?

The `commentsExtended` part declared with
`application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.commentsExtended+xml`,
and the reply anchored in the document at its parent's range, the way Word
writes a thread, so the file opens in Word and the reply appears in the thread.

### Additional information

The runs were part of a document-editing benchmark (30 tasks, five repeats).
Across it, the benchmark's checks judged all 150 Codex outputs completed and
preserved; these five are the only ones with this content type. In two of
them the new comment's reference run also uses a `CommentReference` character
style the document does not define. Both main defects come from the code the
model generated to edit the package, not from a tool it called.
